en: The Sūtra on the Praise of the Merits of All Buddhas, Volume One, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṅkara of India during the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly.
The Master was accompanied by a multitude of one thousand two hundred and fifty people.

At that time, the elder Śāriputra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, readjusted his dharma robes, and took his place to the right of the Buddha. With his right knee touching the ground, he knelt for a long while with palms joined and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Heaven among Heavens!..."
"Are the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones currently present, in good health and ease? And how many are those who are now preaching the Dharma?
When Śāriputra had asked this question, the World-Honored One then addressed Śāriputra:
"Your inquiry is most excellent!"
It brings great benefit and universally benefits all beings.
Listen attentively, listen attentively!
Take this well to heart!
"I shall explain it to you in full detail.
Thereupon, Śāriputra, hearing the Buddha’s consent, was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; joining his palms, he said:
"Yes! I shall listen."
"Listen well; you shall gladly desire to hear it!
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"To the east, beyond thousands of myriads of koṭis of Buddha-fields from here, there is a world named Devatā. In that land there is a Buddha named Ratnasāgara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable numbers of people."

If sons or daughters of good family who hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnasāgara should uphold and recite it with joyful faith and delight, they shall obtain the jewels of the seven factors of enlightenment, all shall be established in the stage of non-retrogression, swiftly attain supreme, perfect, and true awakening, and eliminate the offenses of sixty kalpas of birth and death.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In the eastern direction there is a world named Ratnasamuccaya. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnottama Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable people."

If there are those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnaketu, uphold and recite it with joyful faith and delight, and prostrate themselves on the ground in worship—would the merit obtained by someone who were to take a trichiliocosm filled with the seven treasures and offer it as a gift for a full hundred years be great?
Śāriputra said,
“Very much, very much, O God among Gods!
The Buddha said:

"If there were someone who, upon hearing the name of the Tathāgata Ratnaśrī, were to uphold, recite, and pay homage to it, the merit of this would surpass the merit of giving by a factor of ten trillion."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of Jewel Accumulation (Ratnasaṃcaya), passing beyond eight hundred Buddha-fields, there is a world named Jewel Supreme (Ratnottama). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy Protector, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, upholds it, recites it, and with a pure mind feels joy, faith, and delight, shall eliminate the offenses of five hundred kalpas of birth and death.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system Jewel Most Excellent, passing through a thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Radiance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy of Offerings, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Jewel Radiance, upholds and recites it, and with joy, faith, and delight, they shall attain complete liberation from the three miserable realms.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World of Radiance, passing through fifteen hundred Buddha-fields, there is a world named Dhvajapatākā. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnadhvajapatāka Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable numbers of people."
Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Ratnaketu-dhvaja, upholds it, recites it, and contemplates it with joy, faith, and delight, that person shall thereby accomplish the treasure of the Dharma.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this Dhvajapatāka world, beyond two thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Sarvaguṇaprabhāsa. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavān; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, delivering immeasurable beings."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Jewel Radiance, upholds it, recites it, reads it, and with joy, faith, and delight, prostrates themselves on the ground in worship, they shall eliminate the karmic offenses of birth and death for two hundred thousand kalpas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World of Many Virtues, passing through a thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Sukhāvatī. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is called the Savior who delivers immeasurable beings."
Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, upholds it, recites it, praises his virtues, and further exhorts others to learn and recite it as well.
At that time, Pāpīyān led his fourfold army to where the Buddha was and spoke these words:
"It would be better to cause others to grasp and hold the names of a thousand other Buddhas and encourage them to study them, rather than causing them to grasp and hold the name of Akṣobhya Buddha."

As for those who grasp and uphold the name of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, I shall never be able to destroy their unsurpassed resolve for enlightenment; yet I would also be able to destroy the unsurpassed resolve for enlightenment of those others.
The Buddha said to Māra,
"Whose bodhicitta are you able to destroy?
Māra replied:
“Regarding those who seek the Mahāyāna and uphold the name of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, my heart gives rise to sorrow and feverish distress.
Just as I have today once again experienced this feverish distress because of hearing the name of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya!”
Māra said:
"Furthermore, there are many sentient beings who hold the names of other Buddhas; I may yet be able to destroy their resolve for the path to perfect enlightenment."
The Buddha said to Māra:
"Do not be sorrowful or harbor afflictive fetters; you shall never be able to destroy this unsurpassed resolve for the Way!"
Māra Pāpīyas asked,
"By what causes and conditions?
The Buddha said to Māra:
“You have performed the practice of taking refuge in the merits of all Buddhas while remaining hidden. Why is this?
The Tathāgata Akṣobhya himself shall behold and protect that person.”
Then Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Pāpīyān, why does he today wish to let out a lion’s roar before the Tathāgata, seeking to destroy the mind of right awakening in sentient beings?"
If there are sentient beings who uphold the name of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, as well as the names of all other Buddhas, could Māra truly ever destroy their mind of right awakening?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"I now observe all sentient beings: those who grasp and uphold the names of the Buddhas, and those who revile, scold, or slander them—such persons commit great evil deeds and incur immeasurable sins, entering the Avīci Hell to undergo all manner of suffering."
Śāriputra asked:
"How many are those who slander this sutra?
The Buddha said:

"When the Buddhas of the ten directions extensively preach the Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, they all first praise the name and the merits of Tathāgata Akṣobhya; those sentient beings who hear of these merits never tire of them."

If there are sentient beings who behold the Tathāgata and hear of his merits, none among them would ever dare to slander this sutra. It is not that the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not appear in the world during times of the five turbidities and evil; rather, it is as I am now, acting as a Buddha here within this Sahā world among these inferior and debased sentient beings.
"The land of Akṣobhya Buddha is most sublime and pure; it shall never be otherwise!

You should know, Śāriputra, that as this honored Wheel of Dharma is distributed in succession throughout villages, towns, and cities, sons of good family or daughters of good family who practice with single-minded faith and conduct should widely proclaim these various sūtra teachings."
“You should know this, Śāriputra!
Listen attentively now as I explain the retribution for those who, upon hearing this sutra, slander and disparage it!
Śāriputra said:
“Yes! We shall listen attentively.
The Buddha said:
"In the kingdom of Gandhāra, there are a full hundred thousand people who slander this sutra; having committed such evil deeds, they shall fall into the great Avīci hell.

Furthermore, in the north there is a kingdom named Kaśmīra, where the teachings of the sutras flourish and endure for a long time; yet within that country, five hundred thousand people slander these sutra teachings, and these sentient beings, upon death, shall fall into the great Avīci hell."
Śāriputra! Among the gathered assembly, there will be those who collectively slander this sutra; eighty thousand people shall fall into the great Avīci hell.
In the eastern direction, few will have faith in this sutra, while many will perform deeds leading to the Avīci hell; hundreds of thousands of people shall die and enter the great Avīci hell.
Two hundred thousand people in the south shall slander this sutra and, upon death, enter the great Avīci hell;
one million people in the west shall slander this sutra and, upon death, fall into the great Avīci hell.
"You should know, Śāriputra!

The wisdom of the pratyekabuddhas cannot measure the wisdom of the Tathāgata; how much less so for the śrāvakas and all sentient beings who have not yet attained the fruit of the Path and are adrift in the waters of birth and death—there has never been anyone who could fathom the wisdom and merit of the Tathāgata!"
Now, one who is wise should reflect to themselves:

"The merits of the Buddhas are immeasurable; the wisdom of the Buddhas is inconceivable. The Buddhas have already perfected all-encompassing knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) and the threefold penetration (*trividha-pratisaṃvid*) without obstruction, whereas I am deluded and ignorant, lacking such wisdom. Since the Buddhas have attained omniscience, they alone shall know that which I do not understand."

If I do not understand it, I ought not to slander or disparage even a single four-line verse; how much less should I slander or disparage this most venerable sutra? To commit such a great sin and accumulate a mass of evil deeds would cause me to dwell for incalculable eons within the Avīci Great Hell.
"Therefore, Śāriputra, if sons of good family or daughters of good family should form this thought:

'I have now heard this most venerable sutra and have not slandered it; thus I have repelled the sin of one kalpa in Avīci hell,' they should congratulate themselves with joy and give rise to great exultation."
"For this reason, throughout incalculable kalpas, you shall always be accompanied by this Great Dharma.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the east of this world of Wondrous Joy, beyond ten thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Immeasurable. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Mahāprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is called the Protector of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should anyone hear the name of the Tathāgata Great Radiance, uphold and recite it with joyful faith and delight, that person shall never fail to encounter the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in their future births; they will abide in non-retrogression and will certainly attain the realization of supreme, perfect enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system, beyond sixty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Saṃkusumita. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat, whose name is Amitaghoṣa; he delivers immeasurable numbers of people."
Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound and, with a pure mind, believes and rejoices in it, shall three times proclaim:
"I now single-mindedly pay homage to the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound!"
That person shall obtain immeasurable voices, as well as the pure light-voice of a Tathāgata.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the east of this World of Many Flowers, beyond fourteen thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Free from Dust and Defilement. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, shall eliminate the transgressions of twelve kalpas of birth and death.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World Without Dust and Defilement, passing beyond twenty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Invincible. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Great Renown Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Mahāyaśas, and with a pure mind, faith, and joy, recites it without forgetting, and while kneeling long with palms joined, speaks these words:
"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata Mahāyaśas!"
"If one were to construct mounds of the seven treasures as high as Mount Sumeru and offer them in alms for a full hundred years, would the merit obtained thereby not be very great?
Śāriputra replied,
"It would be very great, very great, O God among Gods!"
The Buddha said:

"It is not equal to someone who, upholding the name and title of the Tathāgata Mahāyaśas, pays him homage; the merit obtained by such a person is hundreds of millions of times greater, surpassing the merit of giving, beyond comparison!"

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the east of this world-system Mo-neng-sheng (Invincible), beyond three thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Prabhāsa (Radiance). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Jewel Radiance, and with all their heart believes in and delights in it, upholding and reciting it, they shall eliminate the sins of ten kalpas of birth and death, abide in non-retrogression, and will certainly attain supreme, perfect, and true enlightenment.
"Those who slander it and those who do not believe in it shall remain in the Avīci Great Hell for a lifespan of one kalpa.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

To the east, passing from this World of Radiance across fifteen thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Many Lights. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, and called the Benefactor of the Multitudes; he delivers immeasurable numbers of people.
Should anyone hear the name of the Tathāgata Mahāpraśānta, and with joy, faith, and delight, recite it without forgetting, they should form this thought:
"By means of this merit, may all immeasurable sentient beings everywhere attain peace and security."
That person shall then receive immeasurable merit and be able to bring peace and security to all sentient beings.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the east of this world-system of Many Lights, passing through seven thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Maṇiprabhā. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Mahāprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Bhagavān; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Mahāprabha and, with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and reads it, that person shall attain the ten powers of a Tathāgata.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of Jewel Light, passing beyond eight thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Rectitude. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Right Sound Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Any who hear the name of the Tathāgata Right Sound and, with a pure heart, believe in and rejoice in it, upholding, reciting, and reading it, shall attain the Dharma of the Tathāgata’s equality of the Four Noble Truths.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world *Ṛju*, passing beyond twenty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named *Prabhāsa-garbha*. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣa-damya-sārathi, Śāstā deva-manuṣyāṇām, known as Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable numbers of people."

If there are those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Amitābha and, with joyful faith and delight, uphold and recite it, would the merit obtained by one who gives as a gift the seven treasures filling the entire great trichiliocosm be much?
Śāriputra said:
“Very much, very much, O God among Gods!
The Buddha said:

"It would not equal the merit obtained by one who grasps and upholds the name of the Tathāgata Amitābha; it would surpass the merit of giving by hundreds of thousands of millions of times, beyond comparison."

Persons of little merit cannot hear the name of this Tathāgata; only those who have established the roots of virtue under a thousand Buddhas shall hear the name of this Honored Buddha, thereby retrogressing forty-eight kalpas of the sins of birth and death.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of Radiant Honor, passing through nine thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Resonance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Moon-Sound Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Candrasvara, and with all their heart believes, delights in, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, the pure merit they shall attain will be fully perfected and complete like the full radiance of the moon; they will be established in non-retrogression and shall surely achieve the unsurpassed, true, and right path.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of Sound, passing beyond twelve thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Peaceful (An-yin). In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Infinite Renown, and with single-minded faith and joy recites it, they should kneel for a long time with palms joined and say these words:
"Now I pay homage to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, Infinite Renown!"

"If one were to calculate the merit obtained by that person—if they were to accumulate the seven treasures like Mount Sumeru and offer them as a gift throughout a full hundred years—would the merit thus acquired not be great?"
Śāriputra said:
"Very much, very much, O God among Gods!
The Buddha said:

"It would be far better to hear the name of the Tathāgata Infinite Renown, to hold that name in mind, and to joyfully pay homage; the merit of this is so vast that it exceeds the merit of giving by a hundredfold, beyond all comparison."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world of Peace and Security, passing through fifteen hundred buddha-fields, there is a world named Sūrya. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sūryacandraprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Candrasūryaprabha, and with a heart of joy and reverence, touches both knees to the ground, kneels for a long time with palms joined, and speaks these words:
"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata Candrasūryaprabha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha!"
That person will swiftly attain the accomplishment of the unsurpassed, true, and correct path.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of the Sun, passing through thirty Buddha-fields, there is a world named Pure (Vimala). In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is known as the Protector of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should any—whether gods, humans, nāgas, yakṣas, or non-humans—hear the name of the Tathāgata Vimalaprabha and, with joy, faith, and delight, pay him homage with a single-minded devotion, all such beings shall attain the stage of non-retrogression and realize the path of unsurpassed, most perfect enlightenment; they shall never again fear falling into the three miserable realms.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World of Purity, beyond half a great trichiliocosm of Buddha-fields, there is a world named Vaidūryanirbhāsa. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Pure Light Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Pure Light, recites that name, and pays homage with joy—whether they be devas, nāgas, yakṣas, or non-human beings—upon the end of their lives, they shall be reborn among gods or humans. They shall never lose the path of gods and humans, shall always encounter the benefit and profit of the Dharma, and their minds of greed, anger, and delusion shall quickly attain purification.
"If there are those who slander and do not believe, they shall suffer punishment for sixty thousand years within the Raurava hell.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

To the east, departing from this world-system of Lapis Lazuli Light and passing through three hundred Buddha-fields, there is a world named Great Abundance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is known as the One Who Delivers Immeasurable Beings.
Should there be those who hear the name of this Buddha and, with joy, faith, and delight, keep that Tathāgata in mind—such individuals are like the orb of the sun;
they are fully endowed with all pure and white dharmas, subdue all Māras and various non-Buddhists, and eliminate the sins of forty kalpas of birth and death.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of Great Abundance, passing beyond ten thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Attainment of the Retinue of Perfectly Awakened Ones. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Immeasurable Jewel Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Treasure, and with a joyful heart believe and delight in it, upholding and reciting it, such individuals shall all attain the seven jewels of awakening; they will be able to establish sentient beings within the most precious state, and the accumulation of their myriad virtues will increase day by day.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of Established Right Awakening, passing beyond five thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Lotus Light. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Most Honored Lotus, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds and recites it, they will be like a wondrous flower in the chamber of the sublime Dharma; their merit and wisdom will increase day by day, just as a lotus flower emerges from the water, and they shall eliminate the sins of birth and death for fifty kalpas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this Lotus Light World, passing beyond a hundred trillion Buddha-fields, there is a world named Universal Deliverance from All Difficulties. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Śarīrapūjya Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, also known as Sarvasattvopajīvya, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Śarīrapūjita, and with all their heart believes in and delights in it, upholding and reciting it, that person shall swiftly cross the ocean of birth and death. They will be able to eliminate the hunger and thirst of desire for all sentient beings, become a noble being (mahāpuruṣa), and act as a field of merit for the world, receiving all offerings from the three realms.

Those who behold this Tathāgata with their own eyes and rejoice with faith and delight shall become great Dharma-teachers for the world; they shall attain adamantine power, establish themselves in non-retrogression, and shall realize the unsurpassed, right, and true path.

If there are women who hear the name of this Honored One, Tathāgata Jinzūn (Body-Venerable), and with wholehearted purity of mind, joy, faith, and delight, free from flattery and deceit, loathe the defiled female body, then from this point forward they shall no longer receive a female body, and they will eliminate the sins of birth and death for sixty kalpas.
"In this way, Śāriputra!

Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Śarīradhara shall attain boundless merit. Therefore, one should seek the path to perfect enlightenment in order to universally rescue all beings and cause them to be free from all suffering."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world, passing beyond the world-system of Many Difficulties and crossing twenty buddha-fields, there is a world named Solid. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Golden Light Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy Protector, who delivers immeasurable people."

Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Golden Light, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind—all such persons shall be protected and sustained by the radiance of the Buddha.
At the time of attaining Buddhahood, one will achieve mastery over the vast and far-reaching radiance of all Tathāgatas and fully acquire all the virtues of a Tathāgata.

Therefore, one should with a sincere heart universally believe in and rejoice in the honored names of all Buddhas; thus one will fully attain the wisdom of unimpeded eloquence, never again inquire into or accept inferior teachings, and all vows and practices shall be swiftly fulfilled.

Whoever hears these names of the Tathāgatas should exhort themselves to arouse a noble resolve and generate a diamond-like will to seek the unsurpassed path; all such persons shall eliminate the sins of birth and death for twelve kalpas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this Sthira world, passing beyond ten buddha-fields, there is a world named Ananta. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Brahmā-Iśvara-Rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Brahmā-Īśvara-rāja, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, and performs prostrations with palms joined, that person shall surely behold that Buddha, become a wheel-turning monarch, establish themselves in non-retrogression, and attain the unsurpassed, true, and right path.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World Without Boundaries, passing beyond two thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Moon. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Suvarṇaprabhāsa, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind—these individuals, in their future births, shall constantly expound the Dharma extensively for the sake of sentient beings.

Although they analyze all phenomena as being like dreams, like the moon reflected in water, and like illusory transformations in order to awaken sentient beings, from that time forward they shall never again fall into the evil realms.
When one gathers together with a great assembly of virtuous ones, they shall always be joyful and able to bring happiness to all sentient beings.
Later, when they become a Buddha, they shall cause the Mahāyāna Dharma to flourish in the world, such that there are no two paths.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this Moon World, passing beyond a thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Fire-Light. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Golden Ocean Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, and called the Worthy Protector, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Golden Ocean, and with all their heart believes in and delights in it, upholding, reciting, and chanting it, they shall attain non-retrogression and will certainly achieve perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? When that Buddha, the Tathāgata, was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this vow:

"If there should be anyone born in my land, or those in other buddha-fields who hear my name, may they all abide in the stage of non-retrogression and attain supreme perfect enlightenment; I shall fulfill for them, to their ultimate completion, the unsurpassed vows of a Tathāgata!"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World of Fiery Light, passing beyond eighteen Buddha-fields, there is a world named Perfect Enlightenment (Abhisambodhi). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Dragon Sovereign King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Dragon Sovereign King, and with all their heart believes in and delights in it, upholding and reciting it; and should, during times of rain, hail, or frost within a commandery, county, or village, place their right knee upon the ground, join their palms in prostration, and speak these words:

"When the Tathāgata Dragon Sovereign King was originally practicing the path of a bodhisattva, he delivered countless dragons from their hardships and perils; by virtue of this merit, he attained buddhahood for himself."
He made this vow:

"Whether within my own land or in all other Buddha-fields, whether while I am in the world or after my parinirvāṇa, if there are dragons who terrify sentient beings with thunder, lightning, hail, or frost, by the power, merit, and wisdom-force of the Tathāgata Dragon Sovereign King, and through the power of this sincere vow, may those who speak these words and prostrate themselves with their heads at his feet swiftly attain liberation."
"Know this, Śāriputra!
Thus one shall swiftly obtain liberation from such calamities; however, one cannot escape them if they are the result of past karma.
All nāgas who hear this Buddha’s name while in distress shall swiftly obtain liberation from their many perils."

Those who uphold the name of this Buddha and further exhort others to recite and maintain it so as to increase their merit shall certainly attain rebirth in this buddha-field; they will seek supreme perfect enlightenment, establish themselves in the stage of non-retrogression, and before long achieve it swiftly.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of Right Enlightenment, passing through ten billion buddha-fields, there is a world named Moon-like (Candropama). In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Sovereign King of All Flower Fragrances, and who, with a pure mind, believe and rejoice in it, upholding and reciting it—wherever such persons are born, they shall obtain the fullness of the fragrance of precepts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; all manner of wondrous fragrances shall pervasively permeate them, and throughout all Buddha-fields, their various precepts shall be perfectly fulfilled, such that they are always able to uphold them without ever failing or transgressing.
Śāriputra said:
"By what original causes and conditions is it possible to be thus?
The Buddha said:
"When that Buddha was practicing the path of a bodhisattva, he made this vow:

'Whether I am in the world or have entered parinirvāṇa, if there are sentient beings who uphold my name and believe with single-minded devotion, they shall all attain such fragrance of precepts as this!'"
"Therefore, Śāriputra, you should always give rise to great reverence and faith toward all Tathāgatas; thus shall these Buddhas protect that person, enabling them to attain immeasurable merit."
If there are those who uphold the names of these Buddhas, they shall obtain them according to their vows; all shall fully attain the wisdom of the Buddhas and achieve non-retrogression.
Kneeling with palms joined, one should personally make this declaration:
"I now pay homage to this Tathāgata King of Sovereignty over All Flower Fragrances!
By constantly recollecting this without forgetting, one shall eliminate the offenses of birth and death for fourteen kalpas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World Like the Moon, passing beyond two thousand one hundred million Buddha-fields, there is a world named Star King (*Tārakarāja*). In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men and Master of the Dharma, Teacher of Gods and Humans, known as the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be any who hear the name of the Tathāgata Śālavṛkṣarāja, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold and recite it, all such persons shall attain the bliss of all dharmas, destroy the armies of Māra, and tear asunder the net of afflictions.

If one hears this sutra and treats it with contempt, slanders it, or uses it for mere mockery, they shall undergo the retribution of their offense by dwelling in the Saṃghāta hell for sixty thousand years.
If there should be one who says:
"I do not believe in this sutra!"
“For seventy thousand years he remained constantly among the hungry ghosts (*preta*), never hearing even the names of food, drink, water, or grain. Furthermore, Śāriputra,

to the east of this Star King World (*Tārārāja-loka*), passing through fifty-five Buddha-fields, there is a world where a Buddha resides, named Vīrabāhu-dhara-dṛḍha-daṇḍa-tyakta-raṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people.”

Any sentient beings who hear the name of the Tathāgata Valorous One Who Holds the Firm Staff and Abandons Battle, and who with joy and faith delight in it, upholding, reciting, and chanting it—even in their dreams—these beings will, like a vajra, subdue the armies of Māra and, by means of various wisdoms, eliminate and overcome all desires.
Those who hear this name of the Buddha and believe it with a single mind will know with certainty within themselves:
"In a former life, we have already seen this Buddha, the World-Honored One, when he was traversing the path of a bodhisattva; of this we have no doubt!"

We shall now give rise to great and solemn vows, never to retreat from the Mahāyāna; instead, we should rejoice in ourselves, leaping with joy as we advance upon the path of the Great Dharma and hear the lineage, clan, and name of the Tathāgata.
The Buddhas universally benefit all beings; they do not abandon a single person when entering parinirvāṇa.
With great compassion, the Buddhas universally pity sentient beings and rain down the rain of Dharma.
"For those who obtain and uphold the names of these Tathāgatas, and who receive them with joy, faith, and delight—I shall now provide you with a brief analogy for the merit they shall attain."

“If one were to take as many Buddha-lands as there are grains of sand along the banks of the Ganges, fill them with the seven treasures, and offer them as alms, would the merit obtained thereby not be great?
Śāriputra replied, “It would be exceedingly great, exceedingly great, and inconceivable!”
The Buddha said:

"If one were to divide a single drop from the waters of the great ocean into one portion, the merit of such giving would be like that single drop; whereas the merit obtained by those who uphold the name of the Buddha is like the waters of the great ocean, beyond all comparison. Persons of little merit are unable to endure hearing this sutra."

If there were someone who has long cultivated the roots of virtue and, upon hearing this Dharma, believes it without doubt; or even if beings in the hells, the animal realm, the hungry ghost realm, or the long-lived heavens were to hear this sutra and thereby obtain great merit—how much more so for one who has already planted roots of virtue! How can the merit obtained by such a person upon hearing this sutra and its Dharma be adequately described?
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this buddha-field, passing beyond twenty buddha-fields, there is a world named Abhirati. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnābhyantaraprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be any who hear the name of the Tathāgata Inner Abundant Jewel Light, and with single-minded faith and joy uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, all such persons shall attain great merit; they will never fear falling into the calamities of the three miserable realms, their vast vows shall be fulfilled as desired, and they shall achieve the aspirations of the Mahāyāna.

Whether in the present or after my parinirvāṇa, those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Abhyantararatnaprabha, and who with faith and joy recite and keep it in mind, shall all attain the joy of the Mahāyāna Dharma to delight themselves, as well as receive the pleasures of the heavens and the human realm; they shall always be born in pure Buddha-fields, where they shall fulfill all their vows in those various Buddha-lands.

According to their wishes, they shall attain parinirvāṇa within the Three Vehicles; meanwhile, from this Buddha’s presence, they shall acquire a mass of merit so vast and expansive that all the various sins committed throughout kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges shall be entirely cast off and no longer experienced—except for the five heinous crimes and the arising of a mind of malice toward the *kalyāṇamitras*.

After these classes of beings have completed their retribution for such sins within the hells over the course of a long period of time, they will, by virtue of having heard the merit of this Buddha’s name, subsequently attain parinirvāṇa within the Three Vehicles according to their wishes.
"You should know, Śāriputra!

Be careful not to commit any evil deeds. As I have explained in the preceding chapter of this sutra, one must not give rise to anger even toward a scorched pillar, let alone harbor malice toward sentient beings;
having established faith in those who have attained the Way, how much more so should one refrain from giving rise to hatred or harboring slander toward the Tathāgatas and their immeasurable wisdom."
Such persons shall remain in the hells for incalculable kalpas, fully experiencing the sins of immeasurable suffering and distress, before they can finally emerge from them.
It is for the sake of those who seek the Mahāyāna with faith and understanding that I have preached this Dharma.

Those who destroy the Mahāyāna Dharma shall truly undergo immeasurable great suffering; those who believe in and delight in it will, as the fruit of their own merit, establish themselves on the stage of non-retrogression and will certainly attain perfect enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world Abundant, passing beyond eighty buddha-fields, there is a world named Most Fragrant Incense. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Fragrance Radiance, and who uphold, recite, and contemplate it with single-minded faith and joy, remembering it until their final thought—these shall all attain the stage of non-retrogression and realize supreme perfect enlightenment.

Once he has attained perfect enlightenment, various wondrous fragrances will issue from all his pores and pervade the ten directions like rising clouds; those who are of inferior character, of little wisdom, or who have studied only shallow teachings shall not be able to understand this sutra.

I, too, with my eye of the Way, behold these various classes of sentient beings; those who have faith and delight in the Dharma of this sutra, having throughout countless kalpas of the past world gathered the teachings of wisdom from the presence of various Buddhas and cultivated the roots of myriad virtues, have now finally been able to hear this sublime and wondrous Dharma.

In the final age at the end of time, those who hear this sacred teaching and believe in it, upholding it with devotion, never giving rise to thoughts of slander, and never having a moment of failing to understand the Dharma, shall eliminate the karmic offenses of forty kalpas of birth and death.

The merit of such a person is like the moon about to reach its fullness; they act as a noble gentleman for the sake of the world, and they ought to receive all forms of reverence, serving as a fertile field of merit for all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world of Fragrance Incense, passing through fifty Buddha-fields, there is a world named Dragon-Jewel Contemplation. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Lion’s Roar Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people."

Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Siṃhaghoṣa, who uphold, recite, and read it, and who with single-minded faith and joy contemplate the practice of the precepts—all such persons shall establish themselves in non-retrogression, achieve supreme perfect enlightenment, become wheels of manifold virtues, enter the pure and white Dharma, revolve therein, transcend the world, and eliminate the offenses of twenty kalpas of birth and death.

Whether they be sons of noble family, daughters of noble family, humans, or non-humans, should any encounter calamities or hardships, they will swiftly attain liberation. Those in the present world who hear this Buddha’s name shall be like a sacred stūpa among all the worlds.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system, the Dragon-Jewel Contemplation (Nāgamaṇi-darśana), passing beyond thirty Buddha-fields, there is a world named Practice (Caryā). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Greatly Powerful, Valiant, and Strong Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Mahāvīryaparākrama, and with all their heart believes in and delights in it, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, prostrating with the right knee on the ground and joining their palms in reverence, and saying these words:
"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata Mahāvīryaparākrama, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha!"

"Such individuals, while wandering within the cycle of birth and death, bring great benefit to many; they attain great power in battle, repel all demons, subdue all non-Buddhists, and eliminate the offenses of twenty-five kalpas of birth and death."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World of Practice, passing through forty Buddha-fields, there is a world named Firm Abiding (Sthitavatī). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Overcoming Transgressions and Abiding Firmly, and with a pure heart believe in and rejoice in it, upholding, reciting, and contemplating it—these shall all firmly abide in the Mahāyāna, attain the wealth of firmness regarding the sublime Dharma, further gain great merit, and increase their virtues day and night, every single day.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system of Firm Abiding, passing through thirty-six Buddha-fields, there is a world named Radiance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Drum-Sound King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Drum-Sound King, and with all their heart believes and delights in it, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, prostrating on their knees with palms joined, and saying these words:
"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata Drum-Sound King, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha!"
If one were to take all the precious jewels that fill the entirety of this trichiliocosm and use them as a gift for charity, would the merit obtained thereby be great?
Śāriputra said:
“Very much, very much, O God among Gods!
The Buddha said:
"It is not as good as for someone to uphold the names of these Buddhas, whose merit is far greater, exceeding the former by hundreds of thousands of millions of times.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

To the east, departing from this World of Radiance and passing through one hundred and fifty Buddha-fields, there is a world named Chamber of Many Virtues. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Moon-Essence Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings.

Should there be those—whether devas, humans, nāgas, or non-humans—who hear the name of the Tathāgata Candrarāja and, with all their heart, believe and rejoice in it; who hear this Buddha’s name and uphold, recite, and keep it in mind—all such shall enter into purity, just as a lotus flower is unsullied by dust or water, remaining entirely free from transgression amidst all evils.

If there are women who hear the name of the Tathāgata Candrarāja, and with a pure mind believe and rejoice in it without flattery or deceit, from that time forward they shall never again receive a female body.
If there are those who lack faith, treat it with contempt, or slander and defame it, they shall remain for twenty kalpas in the Avīci Great Hell, fully experiencing all manner of suffering.
Conversely, if there are those who devote their whole hearts to faith and joy, harboring great reverence, they shall eliminate the sins of birth and death for twenty-one kalpas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World of Many Virtues, passing through a hundred trillion buddha-fields, there is a world named Abiding on Sandalwood Ground. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Surpassing All Flowers Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people."
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“When that Buddha was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this vow:
‘When I attain perfect enlightenment and appear in the world, there shall be no eight difficulties within my buddha-field!’”
By means of this vow, he purifies his own Buddha-field.

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Surpassing All Flowers, and with all their heart believes, delights in, upholds, recites, and contemplates it—such great beings will bring vast benefit to all worlds, like a great king of medicinal herbs.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this Candana world, beyond twenty billion buddha-fields, there is a world named Susthitā. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Lokapradīpa-jyotis Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable numbers of people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata World-Lamp-Illumination and, with all their heart, believe in and delight in it, upholding, reciting, and contemplating it, they shall all be liberated from the calamities of the three miserable realms—except for those who have committed the five heinous crimes or who give rise to malice toward the noble ones (kalyāṇamitra).
"Whoever upholds the name of this Tathāgata shall obtain the treasure of this Honored One’s sublime Dharma and eliminate the sins of birth and death for twenty kalpas.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

To the east, departing from this world-system of Good Abiding and passing through eighty billion buddha-fields, there is a world named Radiance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Śikhin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings.
The reason this world is named "Radiant" is that the Buddha-land of that realm is as level as the palm of a hand, with various lotus flowers covering the entire world;
the radiance of the Tathāgata in that land is brilliant and dazzling, like a great fire constantly shining day and night;
the light of that Buddha-land is majestic, supreme, and foremost, as he constantly turns the honored Wheel of Dharma amidst the great assembly.

Suppose there were a person who covered the ground of a trichiliocosm with gold, further adorned that ground with exquisite garments, and having filled the entire trichiliocosm with these, offered them as a gift; would the merit obtained thereby not be great?
Śāriputra said:
"Very much, very much, O God among Gods!
The Buddha said:

"If there were someone who, upon hearing the name of the Tathāgata Bhūtamati-śānti, would believe and rejoice in it with all their heart, upholding, reciting, and contemplating it, the merit that person would obtain would exceed that of the merit from giving by several hundred thousand times."
These sentient beings, having made their vows with full self-reliance, shall obtain them according to their wishes and eliminate the offenses of birth and death for sixty kalpas.
When they later attain the unsurpassed, right, and true path, their Buddha-lands will be adorned, pure, and blissful, with a majesty and nobility beyond compare.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this World of Radiance, there is another buddha-field named Encompassing Moon. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnacakra Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, also known as the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings; he is currently dwelling and preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system Parivāra, there is a buddha-field named Vijñapti. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is called the Protector of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings, and is currently present, turning the irreversible, unsurpassed wheel of Dharma."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east, beyond this world-system called Awakening, there is a land named Sumeru-flank. In that country there is a Buddha, titled Pure Awakening Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, and Bearer of the World’s Veneration; he delivers immeasurable people and currently dwells there extensively expounding the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world, passing beyond the world-system named Sumerupārśva, there is a buddha-field called Yaśas. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Immeasurable Jewel Flower Radiance Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, and Bhaṭṭāraka; he delivers immeasurable people and is currently present, extensively expounding the wondrous Dharma."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east, beyond this world-system named Fame (Yaśas), there is a land called Sublime Softness (Sūkṣmamṛdu). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sumerukrama Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes; he delivers immeasurable people and is currently present among the great assembly, extensively expounding the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east, beyond this World of Subtle Softness, there is a buddha-field named Abundant Nourishment. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnapadma Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣa-damya-sārathi, Śāstā deva-manuṣyāṇām, Bhagavān; he is called the Protector of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people, and is currently extensively expounding the Dharma to a great assembly."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east, beyond this world-system Abhirati, there is a buddha-field named Padmottara. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sarvaratnasamavasaraṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Bhagavat; he is also called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of this world-system Lotus-Emergence, there is a buddha-field named Golden Light. In that land there is a Buddha, titled King of Trees Abundant Growth Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude; he delivers immeasurable people and currently preaches the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east, beyond this World of Golden Light, there is a buddha-field named Pure. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, known as the Benefactor; he delivers immeasurable people. Surrounded before and behind by an incalculable host of bodhisattvas, he turns the unsurpassed wheel of the non-retrogressive Dharma."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east, beyond this World of Purity, there is a world named Pure Abode. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

These Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently reside in the eastern direction; those who proclaim the names of these Tathāgatas, explaining them in detail and causing others to receive and uphold them, as well as countless others besides them, all currently dwell there preaching the unsurpassed Dharma.

Should there be anyone who hears these names of the Buddhas and, with all their heart, believes and rejoices in them, prostrating themselves with their knees on the ground, kneeling for a long time with palms joined, and universally paying homage to all the Buddhas of the eastern direction while upholding the names of those Buddhas, they should three times say these words:
"I now universally pay homage to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the eastern direction!"
The merit obtained by that person shall be immeasurable.
*The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Praise of the Merits of All Buddhas*, Volume One;
*The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Praise of the Merits of All Buddhas*, Volume Two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṃkara of India during the Northern Wei Dynasty:
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, ten trillion Buddha-fields away from here to the south, there is a world named Pearl.

In that land there is a Buddha, titled Candrasūryapradīpa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Candrasūryapradīpa, and who uphold, recite, and keep it in mind with joyful exultation, believing and delighting in it with a sincere heart and free from doubt, [realizing that] the Tathāgata’s teaching is truly excellent and wholesome—then countless thousands of people, with pure hearts and reverent faith, their emotions stirred by both sorrow and joy, shall weep tears for his sake.
These sentient beings shall naturally remember and know:
"In the past, we have indeed encountered and beheld these Buddhas!

If there are women who hear the name of the Tathāgata Candrasūryapradīpa, and with joy, faith, and delight, from that time forward, in whatever place they are born, they shall never again receive a female body.

In the worlds of the ten directions, whoever hears the name of this Buddha shall all establish themselves on the stage of non-retrogression and will certainly attain perfect enlightenment; amidst all desires, their minds will always remain pure, never entangled by the defilements of desire.

If the people of this buddha-field and the various classes of sentient beings from other directions hear the name of this Tathāgata, their merit will be immeasurable; it cannot be fully described by words, nor can its virtue be exhausted. The retinues of Māra shall ultimately be unable to destroy the unsurpassed resolve for enlightenment of such persons.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“Māra constantly seeks an opportunity to find fault with this sutra and desires to sever its continuity. Why is this so?”
They are bound and entangled by the multitude of desires.

Nevertheless, Śāriputra, among those followers, there will be some in future ages who shall believe in and delight in this sublime Dharma of the Honored One without slandering it; such true persons are like the udumbara flower—rare in the world and worthy of receiving all offerings from the three realms!
Śāriputra said: "O World-Honored One!

In the final age of the end times, when beings are fierce, foolish, and violent, how many sentient beings will there be who are able to believe in and uphold the name of the Tathāgata Candrasūryapradīpa, as well as those who joyfully believe in the names of the various World-Honored Ones and Tathāgatas?"
The Buddha said:

"I now observe this with clear discernment and see that among the community of bhikṣus there is ultimately none [who possesses such qualities]. It shall be the same in the final age when people wear white robes; those who believe in and delight in this sutra, and who recite it, will likewise be few—perhaps only one or two in a million."
Śāriputra said:
"If there were those who hear, accept, and believe this sutra, how much merit would they obtain?
The Buddha said:

“The Tathāgatas have wandered through the five realms of existence for incalculable eons, rescuing sentient beings from the calamities of the three miserable paths, and having fully perfected all their great vows, they appear in the world to extensively expound the wondrous Dharma for the sake of sentient beings; they are truly difficult to encounter, and by means of preaching the True Dharma, they bring benefit to many.”

All sentient beings who hear this shall rejoice with faith and delight; they shall all swiftly be able to understand my wisdom, and their offenses leading to birth and death shall be cast back by a hundred kalpas.
“Those who, upon hearing this Dharma, do not believe or rejoice in it—I see all such as these.
Śāriputra said:
“O World-Honored One, O God among Gods!”
"How many people will slander this sutra, and for how long will they endure suffering as the retribution for their sins?
The Buddha said,
"These sentient beings shall fully undergo various punishments in hell for sixty billion years, because they have slandered the Dharma of the Tathāgatas, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones."
Śāriputra! For how long will this Dharma flourish? In whatever place it exists, foolish people will therein commit acts leading to hell, because they slander the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.

Therefore, Śāriputra, if any wise son of noble family or daughter of noble family hears this sublime Dharma during the final age at the end of time, and believes it without slandering it, they should rejoice and leap for joy, thinking to themselves:
"We have not slandered the Tathāgata’s Dharma; we have already escaped the bitter retribution for the evil deeds committed by our bodies!"
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“In the final age, it would still be easy to obtain the merit of filling the great trichiliocosm with the seven treasures and offering them as a gift;
however, to hear a praise of these manifold merits is truly difficult to encounter. Those who encounter this Dharma are all sustained by the Tathāgata.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this World of Pearls, passing through ten thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Carita-prabhāsa. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sumeru Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-sampanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣa-damya-sārathi, Śāstā deva-manuṣyāṇām, Bhagavān; he is called the Protector of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Sumeru, upholds it, recites it, and contemplates it with joyful faith and delight, prostrating themselves with palms joined, they shall receive the retribution of incomparable merit. The Māra King shall be unable to destroy that person’s unsurpassed resolve for the Way; like Mount Sumeru, it shall remain firm and unmoving. Their merit shall be exceedingly great, increasing day by day beyond measure.
From the world *Cailguang* (in the Dan edition, *Jieguang*), Śāriputra, proceeding southward from here past fourteen thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named *Yinxiang*.

In that land there is a Buddha, titled Mahāmeru Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, also called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people.

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Mahāmeru, and with all their heart believe in and rejoice in it, upholding, reciting, and contemplating it—even if only in their dreams—such persons shall never again give rise to thoughts of anger or agitation toward other noble beings (satpuruṣa), and they shall attain non-retrogression and realize perfect enlightenment.
These noble beings shall understand sublime wisdom and realize that all phenomena are like dreams, thereby averting the retribution for birth and death for eighty kalpas.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south, five thousand buddha-fields away from this World of Sound, there is a world named Purple-Golden (Cāmpeya). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Adhimūla—which in the Jin language means "Transcending Sumeru"—Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people.

If there are those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Atimilū, and with all their heart believe in and delight in it, upholding, reciting, and keeping it in mind—the merit they thereby obtain would be such that, even if someone were to take Jambūnada gold and spread it throughout the trichiliocosm until it was completely filled and used it as a gift in almsgiving, would the merit gained by that person be greater?
Śāriputra said:
“Very much, very much, O God among Gods!
The Buddha said:

"If there were someone who, with a pure mind and joyful faith, upholds, recites, and contemplates the name of the Tathāgata Atimaleya, the merit they obtain would exceed that of the aforementioned gift by more than a hundredfold; it cannot be compared."
"If there are those who constantly keep the name of this Tathāgata in mind, they shall eliminate the sins of birth and death for ten kalpas.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the south of this Realm of Purple-Golden Light, passing beyond twenty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Radiance of Form and Image. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Metaphorically Like Sumeru, and with a pure mind believe in and rejoice in it, upholding, reciting, and contemplating it; and should they prostrate by placing their knees upon the ground, kneeling for a long time with palms joined in reverence—such persons as these shall attain wisdom like a great ocean, be able to fully uphold the teachings of all Buddhas, and swiftly achieve the path of perfect enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south, passing eighteen thousand Buddha-fields from this World of Radiant Form, there is a world named Beyond Pearl Light. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Fragrant Image Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy Protector, who delivers immeasurable numbers of people."

If there are those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Gandhavyūha, and for the duration of a finger-snap, with a reverent and pure mind, they recollect the merit obtained by this Tathāgata—suppose someone were to take Jambūnada gold and spread it across a trichiliocosm until it was completely filled, and then offer it as a gift; would the merit obtained by that person be great?
Śāriputra said:
“Very much, very much, O God among Gods!
The Buddha said:

"It would be far better for someone to recite the name of the Tathāgata Fragrant Image from their mouth; the merit thereof, even for the duration of a finger-snap, is exceptionally distinguished, surpassing the former gift by more than a hundredfold."

Why is this? Because by once raising one's voice to recite the name of this Buddha, one obtains great benefit; how much more so when one beholds the physical form of the Tathāgata with one’s own eyes, pays homage with reverence, or, after his parinirvāṇa, enters a temple or monastery to gaze upon his image, prostrating with devout respect—how could the merit thus obtained ever be fully described!
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system of Jewel Light, passing through countless thousands of Buddha-fields, there is a world named Attaining Heroic Power. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Samantagandhottama (in the Jin language, 'Surrounded by Fragrant Incense'), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Protector of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people."
Śāriputra! That Buddha, the Tathāgata, originally sought the Mahāyāna; while he was a bodhisattva, he made this vow:
"Whatever offerings I have previously made to the various Buddhas, and furthermore, whatever offerings I have made to the Tathāgata, the Perfectly Awakened One, Mijiajianni!"
He burned exquisite incense, the pellets of which were like mustard seeds, and made this vow:

"I pray that when I attain Buddhahood through the merit of holding this [incense] today, the pores of my body shall all emit a wondrous fragrance that pervades worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions; like rising clouds, it shall fill the immeasurable worlds of the Buddha-lands in other quarters, so that all sentient beings may be endowed with the fragrance of the precepts."

When all those who hear my name attain Buddhahood, the fragrance from all my pores shall likewise pervade immeasurable lands; thus, Samantagandhottama Tathāgata shall also personally fulfill and perfect all vows.

"If there were someone who praised and extensively expounded the name and virtues of the Tathāgata, then even if a son or daughter of good family had not obtained food for seven days due to hunger, they should nevertheless go to listen to and extol the Dharma that praises the merits of the Tathāgata."
"Why is this? Because the merit obtained from hearing this Buddha's name is immeasurable.
Śāriputra said:
"So it is, World-Honored One!
Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Samantagandhottama shall obtain merit that cannot be measured; it is indeed exceedingly great!"

In the final age, if sons or daughters of noble family hear of these merits and leap for joy, and furthermore hear the names of the Buddhas and the merit of their dharmas, the King Māra shall be unable to destroy that person’s unsurpassed resolve for enlightenment.
Why is this? Because all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, collectively protect and sustain these sentient beings; therefore, the Māra King cannot destroy their resolve for the path.
The Buddha said:
"If I were to praise the meritorious virtues of this Buddha, sentient beings who hear it might become confused and distracted.
This is because such individuals have shallow roots of merit and lack wisdom, and thus are unable to believe and uphold it."
"Śāriputra, those who have faith should all rejoice,
leap for joy, and congratulate themselves, for these individuals will certainly attain supreme perfect enlightenment.
Regarding the merit obtained therein, I shall provide you with a brief analogy."

All Buddhas, out of their great compassion, desire to lead people into their Dharma. If one were to take the seven treasures that fill the worlds of the ten directions and offer them as a gift, would the merit obtained thereby not be great?
Śāriputra said:
"Very much, very much, O God among Gods!
The Buddha said:

"It is not as good as for someone to hear the name of the Tathāgata Samantagandhottama; the merit obtained is exceedingly great, surpassing that of making the aforementioned offering by more than a hundredfold.
Furthermore, if one prostrates with the five limbs touching the ground, the merit attained will be inconceivable, and one shall cast back the sins of birth and death for a hundred kalpas."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system, beyond ten billion buddha-fields, there is a world named Cloud-Thick Stainless Light. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Pure Light Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy Protector, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Pure Light (*Vimalaprabha*), and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, giving rise to a mind of great compassion for even the duration of a finger-snap; and having wholeheartedly admired and delighted in this Buddha, they say to themselves:

"Now that I have heard the name of this Buddha and given rise to a mind of great compassion for the duration of a finger-snap, by virtue of this merit, I vow that all sentient beings throughout the ten directions may attain the subtle and wondrous wisdom of the Tathāgata!"
"Know this, Śāriputra!

If these sentient beings were to give rise to such great vows, the merit and blessings they would thereby obtain would be like those of filling as many Buddha-lands as there are grains of sand along the banks of the Ganges with the seven treasures and offering them as gifts; would the merit thus obtained not be vast?"
Śāriputra said:
“Very many, very many, World-Honored One!
They are beyond measure.”
The Buddha said:

"It is not equal to that of someone who recites and upholds the name of the Tathāgata Pure Light, who, with joyful exultation, gives rise to a mind of great compassion for the duration of a finger-snap and makes a vast vow; the merit obtained thereby exceeds that of the aforementioned giving by more than a hundredfold."

When you noble sons wish to practice giving, you should perform the gift of Dharma; by this merit, you shall swiftly achieve the path to perfect enlightenment and eliminate the offenses of birth and death for eighty kalpas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Cloud-Thick Stainless Light World-system, after passing ten thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Dharma-realm (Dharmadhātu). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Dharmottama Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Blessed One, who delivers immeasurable people."

Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Dharmottama, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and contemplate it—prostrating themselves with palms joined and bowing their heads to the ground—all such persons shall be able to protect and maintain the Dharma of all Buddhas; the great benefits obtained within the Buddha-dharma will be witnessed by them directly.

For this reason, you should all believe with joy and uphold the names of these Buddhas; furthermore, you should widely proclaim and extol their Buddha-virtues, resolve upon the noble mind of enlightenment, and must not give rise to thoughts of arrogance or contemptuous conduct.
Those who direct reverence and faith toward the Tathāgata are able to extinguish all the sufferings of the three miserable realms; this is entirely due to such merit.

Throughout incalculable kalpas, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have accumulated the roots of myriad virtues and fulfilled the practices of a Tathāgata through true humility and austerity for a duration so remote it is difficult to measure. Only then do they achieve the Dharma-body of a Tathāgata and attain the full realization of perfect enlightenment; indeed, omniscience is truly most difficult to realize.
For this reason, you should not give rise to arrogance; rather, you should all cultivate a heart of reverence and faith toward the Tathāgata.

Suppose the entire world were filled with water, and upon the water was a board with a single hole. There was a blind turtle that raised its head only once every hundred years; for it to happen to pass through that hole would be extremely difficult. Even more difficult, even more difficult, is it to seek and obtain a human body!

If one wishes to eliminate the afflictions of the eight difficulties within this world, and if there are those who hear this sutra and its Dharma, all such hardships and evil realms will be forever severed.
For this reason, you should resolve to make a great vow to seek the most honored and peerless Dharma!
