If one directs even a single thought toward the Tathāgata with a joyful heart and faithful delight, such persons will swiftly draw near to the path of perfect enlightenment and eliminate the sins of birth and death for twenty kalpas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Dharma-realm, beyond fifty-five thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Star Sovereign King (*Tārā-viśeṣa-rāja*). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Fragrance Sovereign King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata King of Sovereign Fragrance, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, kneeling long with palms joined, and speaks these words:

"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, King of Sovereign Fragrance; may he arouse great compassion and maintain this mass of merit, so that all Tathāgatas and their disciples may long enjoy celestial bliss as well as the bliss of the Dharma, and may it be so for all sentient beings."
"If there were someone who did not long for nirvāṇa, such persons would all abide in non-retrogression and swiftly attain perfect enlightenment!
If one were to fill the three-thousandfold world system with the seven treasures and offer them as a gift for a full thousand years, would the merit obtained thereby be great?"
Śāriputra said:
“It is very much so, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

"It would be far better for someone to hold the names of these Buddhas and give rise to a mind of great compassion; the merit gained would be exceedingly vast, surpassing the virtue of making material offerings by more than a hundredfold, and it would eliminate the offenses of birth and death for thirty kalpas."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system, Star Sovereign King (Jyotirīśvararāja), passing beyond ten thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Rectitude and Truth (Saddharma). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Mahāsannipāta Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men and Gods, Teacher of Devas and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Mahāsannipāta and, with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind—such persons shall always be in union with all the Buddhas' Dharmas, nor will they give rise to the intention to enter nirvāṇa.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world of True Reality, passing through eight thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Vast and Expansive (Prabhūtaratna). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Fragrant Radiance Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Fragrant Radiance, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, shall all attain non-retrogression and realize supreme perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? When the Tathāgata Fragrant Radiance was formerly traversing the path of a bodhisattva, he made this vow:
"When I become a Buddha, all sentient beings who hear my name shall attain non-retrogression and swiftly achieve perfect enlightenment."
"May you swiftly attain liberation from within the terrors of the three miserable realms!

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the south of this world Vast and Broad (Prabhūtaratna), passing beyond twenty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Vast and Remote (Vipula). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Fire-Light Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, and called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Fire-Light, and who with joy, faith, and delight uphold and recite it, shall all obtain limitless merit.
Those who slander it and do not believe shall incur immeasurable sin.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the south, far beyond this world-system of Vast Distance, after passing through fifteen thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Boundless Limit. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Any sentient beings who hear the name of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Light and, with wholehearted purity of mind, feel joy and faith, shall be protected and sustained by the radiant majestic power of this Tathāgata; they will cast back the sins of birth and death for ten kalpas.
"Those who slander and do not believe shall remain for twenty kalpas in the Pratāpana hell.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the south of this world-system, beyond the boundless limits, crossing over twenty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Sthira. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Kāśyapa-prabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-sampanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Bhagavān; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, delivering immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Kāśyapaprabha, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds and recites it, the hosts and armies of Māra shall be unable to destroy that person’s resolve for the path.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Sārthavāha world, passing beyond two thousand five hundred buddha-fields, there is a world named Musāragalva. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Candrālokajyotirasa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, known as Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Those who hear the name of this Buddha, uphold it, recite it, and keep it in mind—all such persons shall become guides for the world and shall receive the offerings of the world; these individuals hold the firm staff of the heavens.
"You should know, Śāriputra!
Wherever these names of the Buddhas exist—in commanderies, districts, hamlets, villages, or various kingdoms and towns—they are divine stūpas!"
Why is this so? Śāriputra!

In the final age at the end of time, it is extremely difficult to encounter these noble beings (mahāsattvas) who bear the name of Perfectly Enlightened One (samyaksaṃbuddha). Those who hear of them should all rejoice and, with a single mind, believe in and delight in them.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Lapis Lazuli World, passing through eight thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Sublime Fragrance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sun-Moon Light Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy Benefactor, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Candraprabha and, with joyful faith and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it—whether hearing it or speaking of it in dreams, or passing it on to one another—all such people shall leap for joy and receive the retribution of immeasurable merit. Their resolve for the Way shall be as firm as Mount Sumeru, unshakable and indestructible by any of the Māras.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this World of Wondrous Fragrance, beyond ten thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Sun. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Candrasūryaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, known as Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people."
In that Buddha-land there are no four paths.
What are these four?
There are no hells, hungry ghosts, animals, or those who are impoverished and lowly.
When that Buddha, the World-Honored One, was originally seeking the Way, he made this vow:

"If, when I have attained Buddhahood or after my parinirvāṇa, there are sentient beings who hear my name, they shall all dwell in the stage of non-retrogression and swiftly accomplish the unsurpassed, true, and correct Way. Furthermore, I shall cause these beings to establish their own lands, so that the fields for the unsurpassed Way and all their aspirations shall be fulfilled, just as all my own manifold vows have been completely satisfied!"

"Śāriputra! If there are those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Candraprabha, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, these sentient beings shall likewise fulfill their vows for the unsurpassed path, just as this World-Honored One has."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system of the Sun, passing eighteen thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Golden Pearl Radiance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Fire-Light Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy Benefactor, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be any who hear the name of the Tathāgata Fire-Light, and with faith, joy, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind—they have already held aloft the torch of wisdom and shall cross over the entire ocean of birth and death.
Each of you should apply yourselves with diligence and practice with single-minded faith;
constantly mindful day and night, do not harbor doubt or succumb to indolence;
you should widely proclaim and transform others, establishing the gift of Dharma.
Not even all the Māras can destroy the human resolve for enlightenment in such a person, much less could any non-Buddhist (tīrthika) disparage it!
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south, passing from this World of Golden Pearl Radiance across sixteen thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Mirror Reflecting All Forms and Colors. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Jiyin (Gathering Sound) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, known as the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings.

Any sentient beings who are about to be born, or have already been born, in that Buddha-field—these noble beings surpass all humans and devas in appearance; their features are adorned and their countenances are upright, exquisite, and sublime, with a towering radiance such as is not possessed by the bodies of gods or worldly men.

Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Saṃghaghoṣa and, with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, will in their future births always be upright and handsome, possess a wondrously beautiful countenance, have a mind constantly filled with joy, and have faith and delight in all Buddhas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this World of Various Forms and Images, passing beyond thirteen thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Saṃghāṭa. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Most Majestic Dignity Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men and Master of the Dharma, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable numbers of people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Most Majestic Dignity, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, that person shall become the most honored in the world, revered by devas, nāgas, and spirits, and shall eliminate the offenses of twenty kalpas of birth and death.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system Saṃghāṭa, passing beyond one hundred thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Vijitāvativikrānta. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Prabhāsa-garbha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣa-damya-sārathi, Śāstā deva-manuṣyāṇām, designated as the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be any who hear the name of the Tathāgata Glorious Light, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind—whether they be devas, humans, yakṣas, or spirits—these sentient beings shall, by virtue of this merit, surely attain the path of perfect enlightenment and eliminate the offenses of thirty kalpas of birth and death.
"If there are those who disparage it with contempt and do not believe, they shall remain for eighty thousand years in the great niraya, fully experiencing manifold sufferings.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

To the south, passing from this world-system of Supreme Battle Beyond Limits and crossing five thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named All Sounds. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Lotus Army Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people.
If there are those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Padmavīra, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind—
if someone were to take a great trichiliocosm filled with precious jewels and offer them as a gift, would that person’s merit not be very great?
Śāriputra said:
“Very many, very many, World-Honored One!
They are beyond measure.”
The Buddha said:

"It is not as great as the merit obtained by someone who upholds, recites, and contemplates the name of the Tathāgata Padmākṣa; this merit surpasses the merit of giving, and such a person shall always be in the company of all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones."
"O Śāriputra! You and your followers are not yet fully capable of bearing the hearing of these merits.

This Buddha, the World-Honored One, has for a long time cultivated all the roots of virtue within various meditative concentrations. Any who believe in and uphold the name of this Buddha shall all transcend the triple world, just as a lotus flower emerges from the water."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this World of Sound, passing beyond twenty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Moonlight. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Lotus Sound Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
Śāriputra! For what reason is this Honored Tathāgata named Padma-ghoṣa?

When he first ascended to the site of enlightenment and sat upon a lotus flower to attain supreme perfect awakening, countless devas in the midst of the void raised their voices in unison, singing together:
"The Buddha Padma-ghoṣa has now appeared in the world; his voice is heard throughout the great trichiliocosm!
For this reason, he is named Padma-ghoṣa.
Should anyone hear the name of this Buddha and, with joy, faith, and delight, kneel long and join their palms, saying these words:
"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padma-ghoṣa!

Those who do so shall never fall into the evil realms; they shall traverse all fears and difficulties and swiftly attain liberation, with the sole exception of those who have committed the five heinous crimes.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Moonlight World, passing beyond thirty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Devendra. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnagarbha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, and called the Benefactor who delivers immeasurable beings."
Śāriputra! For what reason is that Buddha, the World-Honored One, named Prabhūtaratna?

When he was formerly traveling upon the path of a bodhisattva, there were incalculable multitudes of śrāvakas who all came to follow him and receive the teachings of the sūtras. With one voice and in unison, they spoke these words:
"This upright person is truly capable of possessing such a profound and wondrous treasure of the Dharma!
For this reason, he was named Prabhūtaratna (Much Treasure).
If sons or daughters of good family should hear the name of this Buddha and, with joy, faith, and delight, kneel for a long time with palms joined, reciting his name three times:
"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhūtaratna!
Wherever that person is born among the Buddha-fields, their mind will always understand all dharmas.
Why is this? When this Buddha, the World-Honored One, was a bodhisattva, he made this vow:
"May such people as these become the Dharma-treasure themselves, and may they take that treasure as their retinue!"
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south, beyond twenty thousand Buddha-fields from this World-Sphere of Heavenly Sovereignty, there is a world named Lotus. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Siṃhanāda Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Siṃhanāda, and with joy, faith, and delight, kneels for a long time with palms joined and raises their voice three times, saying:
"I now pay homage to this Tathāgata Siṃhanāda, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha!"

"In whatever place these individuals are born, they shall all be able to let out the lion’s roar, causing the sound of the Dharma to resound throughout the three thousandfold world system; they shall transform and deliver immeasurable classes of sentient beings and eliminate the offenses of birth and death for fifty kalpas."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Lotus World, passing through ten thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Uṣabhā. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Siṃhaghoṣa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people."

Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Siṃhasvara and, with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, shall, in their future births, obtain immeasurable voices as well as the pure light-voice of a Tathāgata.

Why is this so? If one scatters flowers and incense into the void while reciting "Namo Buddha," one obtains immeasurable merit; how much more so for those who behold the images of the Tathāgata in a sacred shrine and scatter flowers and incense with a sincere heart of reverence? Such people are like fine flowers in this world, none of whom fail to be fresh and radiant.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Star-like World (Tārakā-loka), passing through fifteen thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Without-Sorrow (Aśoka). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Vīrasena Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, known as Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Vīrasena, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind; and with single-minded devotion and trust, take refuge in the land of Aśoka, and with a pure heart offer their utmost sincerity and reverent faith to this Tathāgata—all such persons shall attain equal and perfect enlightenment and be able to widely turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.
Why is this? When that Honored Tathāgata was originally seeking the Way, he made this vow:
"When I attain perfect enlightenment, may all sentient beings who hear my name be reborn in my buddha-field, and may they all fully possess the wisdom of a Tathāgata!"

"Śāriputra! If there are those who slander, despise, lack faith in, mock one another, or hold [this teaching] up as a joke, such people shall fully undergo the retribution for their offenses within the hells for a hundred million years."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system of No-Grief, passing through ten thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Vajrasamcaya. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Vajrasaṃkramaṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy Protector, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Vajra-utsāha, and with single-minded faith and joy upholds, recites, and contemplates it—even if they hear this Buddha’s name within a dream—that person shall be able to destroy the three poisons, dissolve all desires, and attain non-retrogression from the teachings of all Buddhas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system Vajrasaṃcaya, passing through a thousand billion buddha-fields, there is a world named Bhīṣmamaṇi. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sarvacaryāsamatikrāntasarvasaṃśayavicchedana Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, known as the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Sarvaduḥkhapramocana-saṃśayacchedaka, and with joy, faith, and delight, recites and keeps that Tathāgata in mind with a sincere heart.

Furthermore, if there should be anyone who speaks this name of the Buddha, and those who hear it proclaim it with a sincere and straightforward mind, free from flattery and deceit, speaking it truly—these individuals shall all be able to destroy the armies of Māra and the various followers of external paths with their inverted views; they shall be able to resolve and disperse all knots of doubt, and will surely attain the realization of the path to Perfect Enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this World of Fearing the Bright Jewel, passing through eighteen hundred Buddha-fields, there is a world named Flower Fragrance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnamahāparivāra Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
Śāriputra!

If there are those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnamahāparivāra and, with joyful exultation, believe and delight in it with a single mind, upholding, reciting, and contemplating it—such persons shall become great treasures for the world and shall turn the unsurpassed wheel of the True Dharma.
Thus it is, Śāriputra!
Those who hear the names of these Buddhas and believe in them with joy shall obtain great benefit; such is the merit they possess!

As for those who fear and loathe the hardships of birth and death, who direct their minds toward the paths of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas—such as these, with their minor vows and shallow wisdom, whose wills are set upon the inferior, and who are unable to endure the sublime and wondrous path—they abandon the vast wisdom of the Tathāgata. This class of people is incapable of believing in or understanding this profound and wondrous meaning.

If there are sentient beings who seek vast and wondrous wisdom, who incline toward all virtues and are devoted to the most supreme and wondrous vehicle, they should, within this Dharma, seek only the inexhaustible treasury. They should eliminate stinginess and narrow-mindedness, give rise to boundless compassion, and desire only to fulfill the wishes of sentient beings. By practicing such giving, they shall obtain inexhaustible retribution in the field of the Tathāgata; they shall eventually understand the wisdom of perfect enlightenment and be able to bestow wealth and treasures upon sentient beings, causing all to attain individual happiness. May these manifold virtues be dedicated to the unsurpassed, right, and true path.
Śāriputra!

Should there be anyone who hears the name of this Buddha, as well as the names and titles of the merits of all the Tathāgatas, and when these are being widely proclaimed, extolled, and explained, if there are those who do not believe and instead slander them, they shall undergo all manner of sufferings for forty billion years within the Karoṣuṅga hell.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this World of Flower Fragrance, passing through six thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Joyful Arising. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Aśoka and, giving rise to a heart of joy, believe in, delight in, and recite it, will remain undefiled amidst the various desires and shall not be obstructed by them. Their minds will be like lotus flowers, unstained by dust or water; they will attain non-retrogression and will be able to bring peace and security to all sentient beings.

When he later attains perfect enlightenment, if there are sentient beings who hear his name and recite it with a sincere heart, rejoicing with faith and delight—whether during his lifetime or after his parinirvāṇa—these individuals shall also obtain the most extraordinary and wondrous vehicle and become teachers of the world;
they shall all attain immeasurable merit, and in whatever place they are born, they shall never fail to encounter a Buddha.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system *Ratnoccaya*, passing beyond twenty thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named *Karṇa-varṇa*. In that land there is a Buddha named *Dharanimdhara-utsada-tathāgata*, an Arhat, a Samyak-saṃbuddha, one perfected in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed leader, a charioteer of men and gods, a teacher of devas and humans, called the 'Blessed One,' who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Earth-Power-Sustaining-Leap, and with a pure heart and joyful mind, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, prostrating themselves on the ground in worship and mindful of that Tathāgata for one day and one night—this person shall attain the stage of non-retrogression, becoming as immovable as the earth; no māras whatsoever shall be able to destroy their resolve for the path; they shall attain immeasurable wisdom like the great ocean, sever the road of birth and death, and eliminate the karmic offenses of twenty kalpas of birth and death.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system Sāvarṇika, passing through fourteen buddha-fields, there is a world named Deva. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Most Exultant Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Most Exultant, they shall rejoice with great exultation, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind; kneeling for a long time with palms joined, they shall pay homage and speak these words:
"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Most Exultant!"

"These sentient beings shall be sustained by the most extraordinary and wondrous Mahāyāna, and they will also be able to benefit all living beings, such that the three miserable realms and the eight difficulties shall be forever eliminated."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Sahā world-system, passing through eight thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Candanaprabhā. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sovereign King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Worthy Protector, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Sovereign King, they will increase their faith and joy; if they further exhort one another to uphold this Buddha’s name, all such persons shall obtain immeasurable merit.
Śāriputra!

If there are gods, humans, nāgas, yakṣas, or any non-humans who, at the time this name of the Tathāgata is spoken, hear it, all of them shall attain non-retrogression from the path of true and perfect enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this Candanaprabhā world, beyond twenty billion buddha-fields, there is a world named Sarvavādya-prakampita. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat, whose name is Anantaghoṣa; he delivers immeasurable numbers of people."
Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Sound and, with joy and faith, delights in the Tathāgata’s merits, should make this vow:
"By these merits, may I come to understand the wisdom of the Tathāgata!"
"All of these shall abide on the stage of non-retrogression and will certainly attain the unsurpassed, true, and correct path. Why is this?
Because when this Honored Tathāgata was a bodhisattva, he gave rise to great and vast vows and established this aspiration."
If there are those who do not believe and instead slander [this teaching], they shall undergo manifold sufferings for a long time within the hells;
once their retribution is exhausted and they emerge, they will constantly be born in places where they do not encounter the era of a Buddha.
Śāriputra! For what reason is that buddha-world named "Trembling with the Sound of Music"?

When the Buddha Immeasurable Sound originally descended from Tuṣita Heaven, he first produced the sounds of all manner of music, universally vibrating and elevating those musical tones such that they could not be matched by any music, whether celestial, worldly, or even that of non-humans.
During that Buddha’s lifetime, he dwelt in the world, teaching the Dharma and transforming sentient beings until his parinirvāṇa;
in that buddha-field, the sounds of musical instruments were continuous, beautiful, and resonant, vibrating throughout twenty buddha-fields in the ten directions.
For this reason, he is called Immeasurable Sound.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the south of this world-system 'Trembling with All Musical Instruments,' passing through three hundred billion buddha-fields, there is a world named Accumulated Radiance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Dīpaṃkara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, and called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Śāriputra! That Honored Tathāgata abides in radiance, illuminating other Buddha-lands; throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of worlds, he is always present with great brilliance. For this reason, he is named Dīpaṃkara (The Lamp-Lighter).

Those who hear the name of this Buddha and, with single-minded faith and joy, leap for gladness without any thought of flattery or deceit—these shall be protected and sustained by the light of the Tathāgata.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the south of this world-system of gathered light, passing beyond eighty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named All-Fragrance. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnārcis Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavān; he is called the Benefactor who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnaprabhāsa and, with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, these individuals shall all become great treasures for the world and abide in non-retrogression on the path of true and perfect enlightenment.
In whatever place they are born, they shall always encounter the era of a Buddha and never be born where no Buddha dwells.
While traversing the path of a bodhisattva, they shall eliminate the karmic offenses of birth and death for fifty kalpas.
Therefore, Śāriputra, you should not give rise to anger or agitation toward the bodhisattvas or the disciples; rather, you should cultivate a mind of great compassion and revere them.
You should seek the vast and wondrous wisdom of the Tathāgata, and resolve upon the great vow to advance toward the Mahāyāna.
Śāriputra! Such a person will swiftly draw near to the unsurpassed, true, and correct path, and extensively expound the profound and wondrous Dharma of the Tathāgata.

Suppose there were someone who has not yet entered *nirvāṇa* and remains within the realm of a bodhisattva, yet does not believe in the Buddha-dharma, nor believes that there is such a thing as practicing the bodhisattva path, saying that the Buddha-way is difficult to attain.
Such a person shall remain in hell for a full thousand years, fully experiencing all manner of punishments.
Therefore, Śāriputra,
one should not give rise to thoughts of anger even toward insects or worms, much less harbor evil intentions toward the noble ones (satpuruṣas).
Those who are shrouded by the hindrance of delusion and lack shame or remorse further solidify their hellish deeds through slander and revilement therein.

Śāriputra, the appearance of Buddhas in the world is extremely rare, exceedingly rare; though hundreds of billions may resolve to seek the Way, those who attain it when the time comes are but one or two.
"Know this, Śāriputra!
The Tathāgata appears in the world as rarely as the udumbara flower; he appears only from time to time and is not easily seen.

Those who seek the Mahāyāna and have given rise to great vows—whether they have already done so, are about to do so, or are doing so now—and who give rise to a courageous mind free from sinking or doubt, shall before long swiftly fulfill their aspirations, extensively bestowing the food of the Dharma and perfecting the path of right awakening."
In this way, the Buddhas of the southern direction are beyond measure and calculation; they currently abide in peace and permanence, extensively expounding the Dharma.

Should there be anyone who hears this and extensively expounds, promotes, and praises the immeasurable merits of the Tathāgatas, that person should face the south, prostrate themselves with their five limbs touching the ground, mindfully recollect all the Tathāgatas, and pay homage by invoking their names. The merit such a person attains shall be immeasurable.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Glorification of the Merits of All Buddhas, Scroll Middle;
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Glorification of the Merits of All Buddhas, Scroll Lower.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṅkara of India during the Northern Wei Dynasty.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the west of here, beyond a hundred thousand myriads of koṭis of Buddha-fields, there is a world named Sukhāvatī.

In that land dwells a Buddha named Amitābha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

If there are those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Amitāyus and, with single-minded faith and joy, uphold, recite, and contemplate it, they should give rise to vast, far-reaching, and immeasurable joy and establish their minds therein. If they cause their true Dharma-faith to reach one hundred trillion levels as they mindfully contemplate this Tathāgata, such persons shall obtain immeasurable merit, forever distance themselves from the calamities of the three miserable realms, and after the end of their lives, all shall be reborn in that Buddha-field.

When their lives are about to end, those who with single-minded faith and joy keep Amitābha Buddha in mind without forgetting or abandoning him, will have the Buddha and his assembly of monks appear before them; even Māra shall ultimately be unable to destroy such a resolve for perfect enlightenment.

Why is this? Because that Buddha, the World-Honored One, has given rise to great compassion, vowing to deliver all immeasurable sentient beings, and likewise protects and sustains all sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Those who are born in the world of Sukhāvatī shall therein fulfill the wisdom of the Tathāgata’s perfect enlightenment.

Śāriputra, regarding the original vows sought by that Buddha, World-Honored One: those who seek the foremost vehicle shall, in that world, fulfill all the dharmas of the Tathāgatas and Buddhas, and be endowed with the factors of perfect enlightenment.
Those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas shall attain arhatship in that buddha-field.
As for those who are reborn in that buddha-field, they shall fulfill their respective aspirations according to the Great or Small Vehicle.

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Amitābha for the last time and praises its description, believing it without doubt, they should give rise to a heart of reverence and keep it in mind with utmost sincerity, as they would remember their own parents.
They formed this thought:
"May all these beings fully realize their manifold aspirations in that Buddha-land.

As for those who do not believe, who fail to praise and extol the name and merits of Amitābha Buddha, and instead slander him—they shall fall into hell for five kalpas and undergo all manner of suffering.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the west of here, beyond a hundred thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Destroyer of All Māras. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable numbers of people."

Should there be those who hear the name of this most excellent Tathāgata and, with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, they shall all be able to subdue all Māras, tear asunder the net of afflictions, and eliminate the sins of birth and death for sixty kalpas.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, to the west of here, beyond a hundred thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Subduer of All Māras. In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should anyone hear the name of the Tathāgata Saṃghasvara, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and contemplate it, that person shall obtain the voices of all Tathāgatas and Buddhas. Amidst the great assemblies where the Dharma is extensively preached, they shall be preeminent and honored; they shall repel all Māras and subdue them through virtue, and they shall eliminate the offenses of birth and death for eighty kalpas.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Ajita knelt with palms joined and stepped forward to address the Buddha, saying:

"Is there perhaps one matter by which a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, within this matter, fulfills the Mahāyāna vow, abides in non-retrogression, and swiftly attains unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment?"
The Buddha said: "There is, Ajita!"

In the north there is a world named Abhirati; in that land there is a Buddha, titled King of Inner Virtue and Abundant Adornment Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, also called the Benefactor who delivers immeasurable beings.

Should there be anyone who hears the name of this Buddha, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, contemplates, and pays homage to it, that person shall all attain non-retrogression, swiftly accomplish the unsurpassed, true, and correct path, and eliminate the offenses of birth and death for one hundred million kalpas.
Ānanda, those who have made offerings to five thousand Buddhas—only such people as these shall hear the name of the Tathāgata King of Abundant and Majestic Virtue.
Those who hear his name shall, from that time forward, in every place where they are born, always obtain the divine eye; there shall never be a time when they do not possess the divine eye.
He was always able to hear clearly, never failing to possess the divine ear;
he was always able to fly, never failing to possess the power of the divine feet;
and until his final nirvana, he was always of upright appearance, never receiving an ugly or deformed form.
Until their final nirvāṇa, they shall always be honored and noble, never being born in inferior states; until their final nirvāṇa,
they will be able to completely destroy the bonds of all desires, and the six faculties of such persons— eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind— will never suffer from affliction.
Up until their final nirvana, they have never been born in places where there is no Buddha, nor have they ever encountered obstacles that prevented them from hearing the Great Honored One’s Dharma;
nor have they ever encountered obstacles that prevented them from seeing the Sangha;
furthermore, they have never been born in any of the eight unfavorable conditions.
Their precepts are always complete, never lacking at any time;
their consciousness and minds are pure, never subject to anger or agitation.
You should know this, Ajita!

"Ānanda! Those who hear the names of these Buddhas, and with a pure mind believe in and rejoice in the Most Perfectly Awakened One—just as one who is thirsty longs for a drink—and who give rise to a heart of faith and reverence toward the Tathāgata; these, Ānanda!"
They are all able to grasp and uphold the most extraordinary benefits of the Buddha-worlds; such persons shall all obtain sublime, marvelous, and extraordinary merit.
Therefore, Ajita!
Furthermore, one should single-mindedly and diligently uphold these names of the Buddhas.

If sons of good family or daughters of good family desire to attain a particularly sublime, wondrous, and pure buddha-field, they should quickly listen to these names of the honored Buddhas, recite their titles, and pay them homage, saying these words:

"I now pay homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor, who delivers immeasurable beings! The King of Abundant Adornment within Virtue!"
Ajita addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O Heaven among Heavens!
Where is that buddha-field located?”
"How far away from here is he?
How much time has passed since he attained Buddhahood?
The Buddha told Ajita:

"Suppose there were a great mound of sand, one hundred yojanas in length and breadth; if one were to take a single grain of sand and place it in a single Buddha-field, and continue doing so until all the grains of sand had been placed in all the Buddha-fields until none remained—then let that number of Buddha-fields be filled with sand."

Furthermore, take the sands from all the Buddha-fields and place one grain of sand in each Buddha-field; continue this until the sands within all those lands are completely exhausted. Then, take the number of these grains of sand and shatter every one of those Buddha-fields into dust.

Furthermore, take one mote of dust and place it in one Buddha-field until all motes are exhausted; yet even after reaching as many Buddha-fields as there are motes of dust, one has not yet arrived at the end.
Those that remain unreached exceed this number by a hundredfold; those Buddha-fields are so extremely distant from here that they cannot be measured.

That Buddha, the World-Honored One, is currently residing within that richly adorned land, surrounded before and behind by an infinite number of bodhisattvas and an incalculable assembly of bhikṣus, as he expounds the Dharma for them.
Seated here, with my physical eyes, I see that Tathāgata extensively expounding the Dharma amidst a great assembly.

That Buddha, the World-Honored One, seated upon his high throne in that land, likewise uses his physical eyes to observe this world, and he also sees me upon my seat expounding the Dharma amidst a great assembly.
Ajita, you should know that if there are sentient beings who,
with faith, rejoice in what the fleshly eyes of the Tathāgatas perceive, they will certainly achieve the path of perfect enlightenment.

All of these are protected and sustained by all Buddhas and Tathāgatas, who cause them to have faith and joy without doubt; they shall all grasp and uphold the profound and wondrous wisdom of the Tathāgata and attain non-retrogression from supreme perfect enlightenment.
Therefore, Ajita!

Should anyone wish to seek this great merit, even if the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system were filled with fire, they should nevertheless enter into it to hear this Buddha’s name and his Dharma of wisdom.
The Bodhisattva Ajita again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Is there perhaps a single dharma by which one may attain non-retrogression and swiftly accomplish the unsurpassed, true, and correct path?
The Buddha said:
"Yes, Ajita!

To the north of here, beyond incalculable Buddha-fields, there is a world named Vajradṛḍha. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Vajradṛḍhavīryaparājitavikiraṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable beings."

Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Vajradṛḍha-vinirbhedin-saṃharaka, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and contemplate it, making offerings with all their heart—these shall all abide in non-retrogression and swiftly attain the unsurpassed, true, and correct path. They shall cast back the offenses of birth and death for a hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* kalpas, remaining far behind them. Such are the immeasurable merits and great vows of that Buddha, the Tathāgata!

In the past, incalculable kalpas ago, when the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara appeared in the world, I heard this name of the Tathāgata Vajradṛḍha-nirghāta-vināśana-pramardana from that Buddha, whereby I transcended the sins of birth and death for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas.
Ajita, you should know this!
Had I not heard the name of this Buddha from Dīpaṃkara, I would still not have attained perfect enlightenment today.
For what reason is that Buddha named Vajra-dṛḍha-saṃhanana-vinirbhedin?

For example, wherever a vajra falls—whether upon a mountain, a cliff, tiles, stones, earthen mounds, walls, or trees—even if it is merely aimed from afar at the place where it is to fall, there is nothing that it does not destroy, shatter, and disperse.
Thus it is, Ajita!

Those who hear the names of these Buddhas, and who uphold, recite, and keep them in mind, will find all their desires swiftly dissipated; the narrow-mindedness of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas will be completely extinguished, and they will quickly achieve the path of perfect enlightenment. For this reason, he is titled the Tathāgata Vajradṛḍha-vinirbhedin-vikiraṇa (The One Who Is Firm as a Diamond and Who Scatters, Subdues, and Destroys).
The Buddha, the World-Honored One, has fulfilled all his vows in this very way!
"Furthermore, Ajita!

To the north, passing from here through hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddha-fields, there is a world named Maṇiprabhā. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnāgni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is the benefactor of the multitudes, delivering immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Ratnāgni, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it—then all such persons who have not yet entered the realm of *nirvāṇa* shall establish themselves in the stage of non-retrogression and swiftly achieve the unsurpassed, true, and correct path.

All the people in that buddha-field who make offerings to the Tathāgata Ratnāgni shall all attain liberation through the Single Great Vehicle; there will be no such names as śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha.
The Buddha addressed the Elder Mahākāśyapa:
"You should know that the virtues of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas are inconceivable!

Fifty hundred thousand Buddha-fields to the north of here, there is a world named Āmalakī-gandha. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnacandraprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Bhagavān; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
Kāśyapa!

If sons of noble family or daughters of noble family should hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnacandraprabha, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, these individuals will, in their future births, attain the samādhi of unceasing right concentration;
and when they are in that samādhi, they will personally see all Buddhas turning the supreme wheel of Dharma and will be able to master and retain the teachings of all those Buddhas.
In whatever place they are born, they shall constantly expound the Great Dharma for the sake of sentient beings;
their eloquence shall be pure and subtle, making them preeminent among the masses;
and whatever they seek or desire, they shall obtain entirely according to their vows.
Why is this? When that Buddha, the World-Honored One, was originally seeking the Way, he made this vow:

"May all who hear my name upon my attainment of perfect enlightenment be enabled to attain this samādhi of mental concentration; from the first aspiration until the achievement of the Way, may they always possess this concentration throughout that interval, never losing it midway."
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered these verses in praise:
"Beyond five hundred thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Akṣobhya.
In that land dwells a Buddha named Ratnacandra, whose radiance is brilliant and most majestic."
Whoever hears the name of this Honored One has already found that upon which to rely;
in their future births they shall attain dhyāna, and their diligence and wisdom shall never cease.

Their fame spreads far and wide, encircled by light; those people see the Buddha within the buddha-field, who extensively proclaims for the sake of all sentient beings the Dharma taught by the Buddhas, the Great Teachers.
All phenomena are devoid of solidity; observing that within all dharmas nothing arises, one should universally extend compassion to all beings and attain mastery within the various dhyānas.
Having already been able to give rise to such an intention, one completely understands that the three miserable realms are devoid of anger and resentment;
having discerned and understood with precision that there is no self, that which is non-existent is not non-existence.
Thoroughly understanding that all phenomena are unattainable, the dharmas that arise within this interval—such dharmas have no abode.
Seeking to understand both the manifest and the unmanifest, these two are both empty and devoid of intrinsic nature; thus one brings forth and reveals the dharma of selflessness.
Non-manifest consciousness is the meaning of emptiness; one should explain this sublime Dharma with careful discernment.
Manifest consciousness may be understood or not understood; both of these revolve around ignorance and wisdom.
Contemplating these two as both pure, one no longer perceives any defilement in all phenomena;
the speaker of the Dharma has nothing on which to rely, having fully realized the perfection of non-reliance.
Just as the moon moves through the sky, The Dharma he teaches has no dependence;
Thus this wondrous Dharma arises here, Without attachment within the triple world.
In the Dharma of the Bodhisattvas there is nothing upon which to rely; one who understands this is omniscient.
To understand this Dharma and explain it to others, one must be able to penetrate and realize the Dharma that is free from dependence.
One who thus discerns with thorough investigation is drawing near to great wisdom;
having heard these words of non-reliance, the wise shall never again harbor doubts or conceptual reckonings.
One who understands in this way is uniquely enlightened in the world with nothing left to consult;
having mastered such great wisdom, they are titled the Most Honored One, the Unsurpassed Being.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

Sixty thousand Buddha-fields to the north of here, there is a world named Long Joyful Pleasure (Dīrghaprīti). In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Bhadraśreṣṭha, and with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, then wherever they are born, they shall be respected and loved by all, and their compassionate gaze shall be trusted and heeded;
whatever teachings they speak, none will fail to receive and follow. Such persons shall all obtain these merits and attain unimpeded eloquence;
and when sentient beings hear the sūtras and dharmas they preach, they shall hear them with joy and faith, and none shall fail to practice them.
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered these verses in praise:
"Beyond sixty thousand Buddha-fields, there is a realm named Long Joyful Delight.
The Most Honored One, Worthy and Wise, who delivers through the Dharma with compassion, that Great Guide dwells within that world."
Most honored and peerless, without equal, you deliver all sentient beings in every lifetime;
those who hear your name become Dharma teachers, and there are none who do not rejoice in the faithful acceptance of your words.
This Great Dharma King, the All-Knowing One, is relied upon and looked up to by immeasurable multitudes;
if any woman hears his name, she shall swiftly attain the relinquishing of her female form.
The defilements are exceedingly deep and boundless; none who have not transcended the world can enter them.
That which has nothing whatsoever to enter—that is the discernment of the truth and the non-truth.
Having realized that these two things are both devoid of intrinsic nature, they are already quiescent and lack any nature;
that which has been exhausted is considered extinguished, and that which is about to arise likewise lacks intrinsic nature.

"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, eight thousand Buddha-fields to the north of here, there is a world named Praveśa. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ratnapadmaprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavān; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings."

If sons or daughters of noble family should hear the name of the Tathāgata Padmavikrāmin and, with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, then in their future births they will possess a countenance that is upright, handsome, and incomparably sublime, such that all will respect and love them.
They will naturally remember the events of countless kalpas within their past lives, fully understanding where they have come from and clearly discerning all the good and evil they have committed.
In whatever place they are born, all who hear their teachings will believe and accept them, and there will be none who do not follow and apply them.
Kāśyapa!

If sons or daughters of good family hear the names and the meritorious deeds of these various Tathāgatas, the Honored Ones and Perfectly Awakened Ones, yet still cherish the female body, such women will not attain liberation even while remaining among women.
"If one is weary of the female body and does not crave its pleasures, and if one upholds, recites, and contemplates the names of the Buddhas, one shall fully attain such virtues as these.
Kāśyapa addressed the Buddha:
"How, furthermore, can one obtain these merits?"
The Buddha said:

“Having severed all name-and-form (nāmarūpa) and exhausted all defilements of desire, these individuals will swiftly attain immeasurable merit; they shall quickly distance themselves from the female body and obtain the full possession of a male form.”
Those who seek to be women will continue to receive female bodies in every place where they are born, thereby defiling all worlds. Therefore, one should abandon the female body;

one shall instead encounter incomparable spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), whose merit increases day by day. Thus, one will personally receive blessings and further benefit others extensively, swiftly delivering all men and women from the midst of their manifold sufferings.
It is like a poisonous tree: wherever it stands, its spreading vines grow and cause much harm; if one can cut down all such poisonous trees, then everyone will attain universal happiness.
The female body is like a poisonous tree; it increases all desires, harms the spirit with its venom, expands all evil deeds, and causes one to undergo immeasurable suffering—all because of women.

If one can sever and cast off the female body, one thereby cuts off the immeasurable sufferings of sentient beings, destroys all evil conduct, closes off the three miserable realms, and opens the gate of Nirvana; causing all beings everywhere to attain happiness, such persons shall swiftly enter the path of the Buddhas.
Kāśyapa addressed the Buddha,
saying, “How can one eliminate the female body?
The Buddha said:
"One should contemplate one's own body and contemplate the bodies of others; understanding that these two things are both unobtainable, within that which is unobtainable there is no path.
If one contemplates the locations of men and women among them, the characteristics of male and female are likewise unobtainable.
If one realizes that these two things are also unobtainable and have no location, one should therein aspire to attain purity."

If one is pure, there is neither grasping nor rejecting; because there is no grasping or rejecting, there is no conscious mind. When one carefully investigates and seeks it, it cannot be found and has no location. One then reflects within oneself:
"Within that which has no location, can one seek to become a woman by means of being a man?"
If one seeks it with earnest attention, the mind cannot be apprehended.
If one understands the nature of the mind and realizes that there is neither male nor female and nothing can be seen, only then does one draw near to the Way of the Tathāgata.

If one wishes to swiftly resolve to remove this female body, one should contemplate the bodies of men and women and realize that there is no distinction between them, nor any duality of increase or decrease. Even when receiving a female rebirth and assuming a female form, if one applies reasoning as it has been taught, one finds that within the six elements (ṣaḍdhātu) neither male nor female can be found. One who acts in this manner is truly seeking the path of the Tathāgata.

Furthermore, those who wish to seek the understanding of such matters, and those who have attained true and thorough knowledge of this Dharma—these two types of people, during the time of past Buddhas, have already heard the names of these various Buddhas.
One should know that such a person, in past lives, performed great meritorious deeds in the presence of various Buddhas; it is now that they hear these names of the Buddhas.
Those who uphold these names of the Honored Ones—who are the objects of reliance and veneration for the world and possess sovereign power—shall obtain immeasurable merit.
Whoever hears this, or whoever studies it, I see them all.
Those who seek it with urgency and obtain this sutra are no different from having seen me.
If there are those who treat such a person with contempt and say, "These are not the words of the Buddha," those who speak thus are slandering the Buddha and destroying the sutras.
Having slandered this sutra, they commit a great evil; by reason of this wicked conduct, they shall enter hell and undergo the retribution of manifold sufferings for incalculable kalpas.

When their retribution for hellish offenses is exhausted and they are reborn elsewhere, they shall always be deaf and mute, unable to speak; their sensory faculties shall be obstructed and never fully intact; they shall always be foolish and prone to madness.

Those who have maliciously obstructed the Bodhisattvas will be of meager merit and ugly appearance, their speech lacking authority, and they shall always be born into lowly stations and always into evil realms.

Wherever they are born, they shall never hear the Dharma; regarding the sūtras and teachings spoken by the Tathāgata’s Perfect Enlightenment, they will ultimately be unable to explain their profound and subtle meanings.

Foolish people who dispute with this sutra will undergo extensive retribution for their sins; strengthening their own deluded views, they disparage this Dharma of the sutra, and such beings shall remain perpetually foolish throughout their lives.

The Buddhas, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, have always acted as the great illumination for the world. I earnestly and repeatedly exhort you all—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—that those who slander, revile, or abuse this sutra and the Dharma shall truly suffer heavy retribution!

The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently reside throughout the ten directions in immeasurable worlds acting as Dharma-teachers; the sutras and teachings they proclaim are truly difficult to hear.

Out of compassion, the Tathāgata earnestly exhorts you all: if there are those who have faith and delight in the names, merits, and dharmas of the Buddhas, they will naturally accord with all wholesome dharmas.
Those who study, uphold, recite, and contemplate them shall swiftly behold all the Tathāgatas; their wisdom will increase further, and they shall attain unimpeded wisdom.
If there are those who encourage others to recite the names of the Buddhas, wherever they are born, they shall travel through the four quarters alone, speaking and walking by themselves without fear.

If there are those who take delight in wholeheartedly revering and honoring these names of the Buddhas, you should know that such persons will never again be far from the path of perfect enlightenment.

If there are those who rejoice in the merits of the Buddhas and further encourage others to study these Buddha-names, wherever they may be, in the realms where the Tathāgatas roam, they shall have no fear or difficulty amidst the various desires.
"You should know, Kāśyapa,
that if a bhikṣu possesses four qualities, he will be able to have faith in these names of the honored Buddhas.
What are these four?"

In past lives, they heard the profound Dharma from various Buddhas; they delighted in quiet, secluded, and pure places; in every lifetime they encountered virtuous spiritual friends; and they did not engage in perilous conduct regarding the Dharma.
"You should know, Kāśyapa, that these are the four matters.

If a bhikṣu is able to possess these, he will have no doubts or difficulties regarding the Dharma of the Tathāgatas' perfect enlightenment; when such a person hears of the merits of the Tathāgata, he will then be able to believe and rejoice in them with a single-minded heart."
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered this verse in praise:
"In the past, they made offerings to the Honored Buddhas;
By virtue of these merits, when their names are heard, Even in the final evil age, those who hear them Will universally increase their manifold virtues through these titles."
Those who in the past have seen various Buddhas, And have heard the profound and wondrous meaning of the Tathāgata,
Whose pure virtues from former lives were free from contention— Only such as these are able to believe and practice accordingly.

If they are enabled to hear the profound and wondrous Dharma, And are taught its various subtle and exquisite meanings, Such people will never give rise to doubt; The Buddha’s profound Dharma cannot be destroyed.
Abiding securely in the meaning of all dharmas thus taught, gather your mind through reflection and place faith in universal wisdom;
with a firm resolve, listen to my words and do not forget this sublime Dharma.
Never again contend with the Dharma, and upon hearing the names of the Buddhas, be able to practice them accordingly.
With mindfulness and non-mindfulness not interfering with one another, there is no distinction within that Dharma;
inconceivable and utterly vast, one never wavers in the face of great wisdom.
Those who seek this Dharma of profound wisdom, who understand and penetrate its deep meaning without needing instruction,
and who diligently seek all profound teachings without doubt—
know that such persons take no pleasure in inferior activities and have nothing further to seek; they possess supreme courage regarding the Dharma.
There is none who does not believe in the Dharma taught by the Buddha;
those sentient beings who, in previous lives, have combined various virtues to receive their karmic rewards, and who are free from contention, are able to hear it.
It reveals the great wisdom and virtue of all Tathāgatas, and serves as praise for the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Those who recite and uphold these names, the Buddhas from afar praise their virtue;

amidst the great assembly, they extol their names. Such people shall always hear the voices of the Buddhas and swiftly be able to comprehend the Dharma of Great Wisdom—the utterly pure karma of non-arising.
Emitting great radiance that surpasses the sun and moon, you extensively expound the wondrous Dharma for the sake of sentient beings;
in a future assembly, you shall attain the most perfect enlightenment, universally illuminating all Buddha-fields.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, above there is a world named Ratnacandra.

In that land there is a Buddha, titled Suvarṇaratnāvabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, designated as Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people; he is currently present, preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa! Above, there is a world named Hastikṣetra.

In that land there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat, known as Amitābhavipula. He now dwells and currently teaches the Dharma, delivering immeasurable people."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

Above, there is a land named Devī-ratna (Heavenly Jade Woman). In that country there is a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, known as Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable people and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

Above, there is a land named Sumerudhvaja. In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Dehashu Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable people and is currently preaching the Dharma."

"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, in the direction above there is a land named Honored Assembly with Few Intentions (*Gauravasaṃghālpamanas*). In that land there is a Buddha, titled Immeasurable Diligence Arising Abundance (*Anantavīryodbhavasaṃpatti*) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude; he delivers immeasurable people and currently dwells preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land called Anupādāna (Non-Appropriation). In that country there is a Buddha named Vāgīśvararāja (Victorious Lord of Speech), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is the benefactor of the multitude, delivering immeasurable people, and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land named Pure Contemplation Adornment. In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Amogha-Abhijña (No Delusion Abundance) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable people and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, in the direction above there is a land named Sunlight.

In that country there is a Buddha, titled Candrarucipūrṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Bhagavān; he is called the Protector of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable beings. He is currently present, preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land called Dharma-Preaching. In that realm there is a Buddha named Immeasurable Light Abundance Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, known as the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people; he is presently dwelling there, preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

Above, there is a land named Ratnavyūha-śīrṣa-kṣaya. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Ākāśābhimukha-prabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, known as Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable people and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land named Suvicitra. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Most Pure Immeasurable Banner Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people; he is currently present, preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, in the direction of the zenith there is a land called Viśeṣa.

In that country there is a Buddha, named Supratiṣṭhitabhadraikarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, designated as Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable people and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, above there is a land named Birth of Diligence.

In that land there is a Buddha, titled Sarvārthasiddhivṛddharāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Bhagavān; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, delivering immeasurable people, and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, in the direction above there is a land named Praṇidhibala.

In that country there is a Buddha, titled Śuddhamatiguṇasamṛddhi Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Bhagavān; he is called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people, and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa! Above, there is a land named *Ratipraveśa*.

In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Pure Wheel Banner Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men and Master of the Dharma, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people; he currently dwells there, preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, in the direction above there is a land named Candanagandha.

In that country there is a Buddha, titled Vaidūryaprabhā-samṛddhi Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, known as Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people; he is currently residing there, preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, above there is a land called Nakṣatra.

In that land there is a Buddha named Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāmin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, known as the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people; he currently resides there, preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land named Abundant with Immeasurable Virtues. In that country there is a Buddha, titled Most Pure Virtuous Jewel-Abiding Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes; he delivers immeasurable people and is currently preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

Above, there is a land called 'Beyond the Reach of Sound. In that realm dwells a Buddha named Ratnārcistūrottaraṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavān; he is also titled 'Benefactor of the Multitudes,' who delivers immeasurable beings and currently dwells preaching the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land named Boundless Eye (*Anantacakṣus*). In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Immeasurable Shame and Remorse Golden Most Abundant Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitude, who delivers immeasurable people; he currently dwells there, preaching the Dharma."
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered this eulogy in verse:
“The Tathāgata’s virtue is like the full moon; The most supreme among all devas, the Honored Hero.
These Great Honored Ones, kings among virtues, Are able to eliminate all calamities for sentient beings.”
The merit of upholding the names of all Buddhas is perfected; it can purify all lands to make them solemn and clear.
It is difficult to encounter this honored sutra, and few sentient beings hear its name.
If one practices with faith and makes offerings, they shall attain great wisdom and powerful strength;
understanding that all phenomena are immeasurable, they shall become a sovereign of perfect enlightenment.
The Dharma of Perfect Enlightenment is profound and subtle; one should not give rise to doubt within it.
One should faithfully accept and honor all Teachers, and with joy and reverence, pay homage without hesitation.

"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, in the direction above there is a land named Jewel Lotus Adornment. In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Lotus Honored Abundance Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, called the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."

Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Abundant Lotus Honored One shall have the three evil paths closed for them; they shall have already attained the flower of the Tathāgata, and among all the dharmas of the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, they shall attain the flower of the Unsurpassed Way, thereby casting back the offenses of birth and death for thirty-six kalpas.
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered this verse of praise:
“In the upper direction there is a land adorned with jewels, Where myriad flowers flourish throughout the great trichiliocosm.
Its radiant colors are so brilliant and beautiful to behold, Like the celestial Nandana grove.”
The Honored Buddha Padma resides in that land; his teaching is peerless and his wisdom thoroughly penetrating.
His light universally illumines the great trichiliocosm; with all marks most majestic and dignified, he is the supreme among sages.
If any woman hears his name, she shall sever the evil paths and encounter the sages;
she shall eliminate the karmic offenses of thirty kalpas of birth and death, and will surely attain unretrogressive, perfect enlightenment.
Not perceiving the body, one realizes the purity of the Way; through successive lives, wisdom and merit are perfected.
By recollecting the Buddhas, one gains virtuous friends; enemies are extinguished and the suffering of sin is eliminated.
One should universally prostrate to these Buddhas, who are all currently present in various lands;
that person shall quickly receive offerings for thus prostrating to the Great Dharma Kings, the Buddhas.
You should not doubt these words of mine; you will certainly attain Buddhahood with boundless virtue.
You shall always join the assemblies of the wondrous Dharma, and later, you will achieve perfect enlightenment with uniquely penetrating wisdom.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa, in the direction above there is a land called Ratnapradīpa.

In that realm there is a Buddha named Vimalaratnasaṃbhava-ṛddhi Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is called the Protector of the Multitudes, delivering immeasurable beings."

Should anyone hear the name of the Tathāgata Pure Jewel Abundant Prosperity, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, that person shall obtain the jewels of the seven factors of enlightenment and eliminate the sins of birth and death for thirty kalpas.
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered these verses of praise:
"In the realm above named Ratnaprabhāsa, The Most Honored Pure Jewel resides in that land.
Whoever hears his name Shall attain the seven factors of enlightenment and dhyāna."
Through the suffering of birth and death for thirty great kalpas, one transcends the past where causes and conditions no longer exist;
having attained incomparable power and abiding in immovability, one shall ever encounter all the World-Honored Ones.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land named Vidyutprabhā. In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Vidyutpradīpapatākārāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, known as the Benefactor of the Multitudes, who delivers immeasurable people."
