Should there be those who hear the name of the Tathāgata Vidyut-pradīpa-dhvaja-rāja, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, all such persons shall be forever far removed from the eight states of adversity and shall never again be born into inferior families.
Then the World-Honored One uttered these verses in praise:
"In the region above there is a realm named Lightning Light, Where a Great Honored One is titled King of Lightning Lamp.
Whoever hears the name of this Noble Being Shall forever sever the eight difficulties and never be born [in them] again."
With wisdom he understands the root of birth and death; Various merits are accomplished in their proper sequence.
He flourishes the transformation of the Way to deliver sentient beings; His wisdom alone penetrates all, O peerless Sage.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

Above, there is a land named Ākāśasāra. In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Dharmagaganapradīpa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he delivers immeasurable people."

Should there be anyone who hears the name of the Tathāgata Dharmakūṭapradīpa and, with joy, faith, and delight, upholds, recites, and contemplates it, they shall eliminate the sins of birth and death for sixty kalpas, attain non-retrogression from supreme perfect enlightenment, and constantly be able to assemble together with all Buddhas. In the present life, they shall behold that Buddha, the World-Honored One, and shall also see this Tathāgata within their dreams.

"You should know, Kāśyapa, that such a person, prostrating with their five limbs upon the ground in this life and directing single-minded reverence toward the Tathāgata, plants immeasurable merit and brings all the seeds of their roots of goodness to full completion. They shall always encounter virtuous spiritual friends and shall always be mutually respected and loved by all people."
"In this way, Kāśyapa, these are the various wholesome rewards obtained in the present life; the merits of that Buddha, the Tathāgata, are all gathered together in such a manner.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One spoke in verse, saying:
“There is a great world-system called Dense Void; its Buddha is named Lamp of Dharma-Voidness.
That World-Honored One’s fame is universally renowned, and his radiance is so vast it surpasses empty space.”
Whoever hears the name of this Honored One shall transcend the sins of birth and death for sixty kalpas;
they will surely encounter and behold the various Buddhas and preach the wondrous Dharma before the Tathāgatas.
Through diligence, one shall see the Buddhas in this very life; one should prostrate with the five limbs to those Tathāgatas.
In dreams, one shall behold those World-Honored Ones, those Buddhas and Guides surrounded by halos of light.
Recalling that the Tathāgata has brought about such merit, one shall always behold those of great compassion;
being born, one shall always encounter the Kings of Dharma, for such a person shall see the Buddhas in this very life.
That Buddha, the Guide, possesses immeasurable virtue; with wisdom universally attained, he is the Dharma King.
Those who diligently seek all virtues should, with their whole hearts and respectful minds, pay homage to that Buddha.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land named *Samyak-vibhakti*. In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Sarvaguṇasamudgatarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, and Bhagavat; he is called the Protector of the Multitudes, delivering immeasurable people."
For what reason is this realm called the "Section of Thorough Truth"?
You should know, Kāśyapa,
that in that world all things consist of eight parts:
There were sections of various flowers, sections of sandalwood trees, and sections of exquisite golden tāla trees.
From that buddha-field issued many kinds of renowned incense, which pervaded the entire world;
in the sky above that land, these formed a canopy of fragrance that universally covered the buddha-field.

When that Buddha, the Tathāgata, approaches the Dharma seat to grace the great assembly, any who hear the name of the Tathāgata Sarvaguṇasamudgata will have their six sense faculties made upright and ever-pure; they will comprehend the divisions of the wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas and eliminate the offenses of birth and death for eighty kalpas.
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered these verses in praise:
"In this world of Certainty there are eight kinds [of trees], Adorned with the fragrance of precious Tāla trees;
Exquisite and famous incense issues forth, pervading the entire realm, While clouds of fragrant canopies universally cover the void."
The Greatly Wise and Perfectly Awakened One resides in that land; his fame is universally renowned and he is called "Multitude of Virtues.
His physical form is upright, dignified, and most exquisitely beautiful; as the Dharma King, he walks alone, fearless and without dread.
Whoever hears the name of this Honored One will achieve a countenance that is upright, marvelous, and endowed with merit;
their limbs will be perfectly formed and square, such that one can never tire of beholding them, and all will not fail to revere them.
His merit is most supreme and peerless; with joy and exultation, he travels through all lands.
His diligence and valor are utterly transcendent, as he eliminates the karmic offenses of eighty kalpas of birth and death.
Never turning back from the path of perfect enlightenment, they are able to extensively expound the sublime Dharma of the Buddha;
attaining all forms of happiness, they shall always be honored and noble in their future births.
Having attained purity without distinction, one contemplates the manifold virtues of the Tathāgata;
reflecting upon the meaning of all dharmas through wisdom, one increases merit and accomplishes all forms of knowledge.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

Above, there is a land named Candrasūryavicitra. In that country there is a Buddha, titled Bhadra-dhvaja-ketu-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, also called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people."

Should anyone hear the name of the Tathāgata Worthy Banner-Standard King, and with joy, faith, and delight, uphold, recite, and keep it in mind, that person shall attain the stage of non-retrogression and achieve supreme perfect enlightenment, thereby casting back the sins of birth and death for fifty kalpas.
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered this verse of praise:
"In the realm above named Moon-Sun Glory, The Buddha there is named King of the Virtuous Banner.
The Great Seer, the Dharma King, dwells in that land, His marks and signs radiant and bright like the full moon."
Whoever hears the name of this Honored One, their faculties will become clear as they traverse the path of birth and death;
they shall always increase in all dharmas and dwell with certainty in the lineage of the Tathāgata.
By recollecting the Buddha with a sincere mind and paying him homage, one shall eliminate the karmic offenses of fifty kalpas of birth and death.
"Furthermore, Kāśyapa!

In the direction above, there is a land named Ratnabīja. In that realm there is a Buddha, titled Sarvaratnavicitravarṇadhara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, called Bhagavat, who delivers immeasurable people."
For what reason is that land named "Jewel Seed" (Ratnabīja)?

You should know, Kāśyapa, that in that buddha-world all sentient beings seek the unsurpassed, true, and perfect path. The bodhisattvas in that land possess courageous supernatural powers; innumerable bodhisattvas simultaneously, in the time it takes to snap one's fingers, fly by the power of their supernatural feet to the ten directions. They pay homage to immeasurable Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reaching them all, and are able to bring all sentient beings to fulfillment.
When this account of the merits of these Buddhas is being spoken, whoever hears it shall have already arrived in the lands of these Buddhas.
Who is able to initiate the practice of great diligence?

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who uphold these names; their names are: Bodhisattva Lion’s Play, Bodhisattva Lion’s Exertion, Bodhisattva Lion’s Banner, Bodhisattva Lion’s Action, Bodhisattva Firm Courage and Diligence, and Bodhisattva Striking with Vajra Wisdom.

Whoever hears the name of the Tathāgata Sarvaratnarañjita-varṇa-dhara and the names of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas shall all attain the ten powers of a Tathāgata and the eighteen unique qualities, shall always be able to turn the irreversible wheel of Dharma, and shall eliminate the sins of six hundred kalpas of birth and death.
Thereupon the World-Honored One uttered these verses in praise:
"I have now declared the Kings of Dharma, All of whom are currently living in health and peace.
The Great Teacher who attained self-awakening without a master, Having attained the bliss of Nirvana, is the most honored."
The name of the Tathāgata is pure by nature; all dharmas and modes of conduct are pure.
Those who hear these names at the very end will give rise to great joy and harbor deep reverence.
Do not harbor doubt regarding the Tathāgata; with utmost sincerity, offer your faith and do not say there is none.
You should know that this Śāriputra, as well as these others, have already made offerings to me in previous lives.
If there are those who have made offerings to the Buddhas, and in their final life, during this world of terror,
they are able to hear these various sublime sutras, they will with single-minded faith and joy give rise to no doubt.
The path traversed by the great wisdom of all Buddhas—without this supreme wisdom, one cannot attain thorough penetration.
Having achieved much within this Dharma, how could one harbor doubts regarding this sutra?
If one encounters a wondrous jewel, a treasure beyond doubt, the fool fails to recognize it and finds it unattractive;
the poor man hesitates, his mind undecided, for he lacks the price to acquire such a treasure.
This Dharma gives birth to the Samyaksaṃbuddhas; all of this is what the Mahāsattvas have heard.
Those of shallow wisdom lack the eye of insight; how could such as these ever believe it?
There may be a wealthy person who has accumulated many treasures;
upon hearing of the wish-fulfilling jewel, he rejoices greatly and praises it, saying that it will greatly increase his treasures, for he intends to purchase it to adorn himself.
Those who possess a convergence of merit and wisdom, upon hearing the names of the Buddhas, rejoice greatly;
they praise them with deep reverence, desiring to hear them, and thus attain the jewel of perfect enlightenment to adorn themselves.
Those who practice evil ways and seek after evil, those who are sycophantic and perverse,
and those whose merit and wisdom are meager— such people will ultimately be unable to hear this Dharma.
Those who are short-lived, perverted, and deluded, whose minds are defiled by excessive stinginess,
and who are confused by lust and hatred— such as these are not fit to hear this Dharma.
Those whose learning is meager, who are indolent, arrogant, and self-deprecating; those with corrupt and evil friends whose minds are not yet matured;
those who are inwardly conceited though outwardly appearing pure—such a multitude is unfit to hear this sutra.
Countless devas and humans then cried out: "The Sublime, Unsurpassed Honored One of Perfect Enlightenment!
How wonderful that this wondrous Dharma is so difficult to hear! We shall now listen to the jewel of the peerless Path."
Among the names of the Tathāgatas that one hears, the benefits obtained are beyond enumeration;
the devas above, in the midst of the void, scatter flowers and incense while sounding the music of drums.
The exquisite fragrances of the devas pervade everywhere; throughout the great trichiliocosm, clouds of incense form.
Radiant light shines universally upon the ten directions, and all buddha-fields tremble in six ways.

At that time, while the World-Honored One was proclaiming the names of the various Tathāgatas, all those present in the assembly saw from their seats these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, each within the great congregations of their own lands preaching the Dharma. They all rose from their seats, paid homage to the World-Honored Ones, and there was none who did not rejoice with immeasurable exultation.

At that time, among those present in the assembly—consisting of many thousands of people, both those who had attained the Way and those who had not—all resolved their minds upon the unsurpassed, true, and correct path.
Bodhisattvas from the worlds of the ten directions, each as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all came to this place to pay homage to Śākyamuni.

Within that assembly, ten million bhikṣus attained arhatship; furthermore, one hundred thousand bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs attained the pure Dharma-eye. Additionally, one hundred thousand people all attained the patience of the Dharma (dharmakṣānti).

Five hundred upāsakas and four hundred upāsikās simultaneously rose from their seats, adjusted their robes, made offerings to the Tathāgata, and all resolved to attain supreme, perfect, and true enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
Thereupon Śāriputra knelt with his hands joined in reverence and stepped forward to address the Buddha, saying:
"What is the name of this sutra?
How should it be upheld?"
The Buddha said:
"This sutra is titled 'The Chapter on Praising the Merits of All Buddhas,' and it is also titled 'The Collection of the Flowers of All Buddhas.'"
"You should practice this!

When the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra, Śāriputra, the bhikṣus, the devas, humans, nāgas, asuras, and the entire great assembly were all filled with great joy; they came forward, prostrated before the Buddha, and departed.
Majestic are the Buddhas of the ten directions;
their lands are exceedingly pure and bright, adorned with the seven treasures and fragrant with the exquisite scent of sandalwood.
They consist entirely of bodhisattvas, and even the names of the two vehicles do not exist there.
I speak only of non-retrogression, the excellence of the path of Prajñā.
The towering Buddhas of the ten directions and the treasures of the paths of the three periods—
those who hear, believe, and delight in them will swiftly achieve unsurpassed truth.
Wandering upon the Bodhisattva path, firmly established and never regressing,
they are always able to see the Buddhas wherever they are born, encountering all the World-Honored Ones—
those towering Buddhas of the ten directions, the guides of the triple world.
With a sincere heart harboring reverence, Believing with joy and free from doubt,
One’s birth shall always be upright, And one’s countenance exceedingly radiant as a flower.
Possessing eloquence and wisdom uniquely penetrating, I vow to pay homage to the Teacher of Gods and Humans.

On the twentieth day of the sixth month in the sixth year of the Linjia era, this sutra was performed at the Jinhua Shrine in the kingdom of Kucha, with the Sanskrit sounds being translated into the language of Jin.

Dharmabhadra was thoroughly versed in the Abhidharma and eloquent in the meanings of various sutras; furthermore, he had exhaustively investigated the matters of the Mahāyāna and could expound upon profound dharmas with great skill, ranking first among those of broad learning in the kingdom of Kucha.
Falin immediately requested permission to produce this sūtra; with his own hands, he took up the Sanskrit manuscript and translated it into the Kuchean language.
At that time, both monastics and laypeople rejoiced and marveled at such an unprecedented event, vying with one another to recite it and praising its merit.
The śramaṇa Huikai was proficient in the Kucha language and well-versed in the sounds of the Jin.

Kumārajīva again commanded him to translate the Kucha language into the Jin language; Kumārajīva himself acted as the scribe for the oral transmission. Although the phrasing and sentences were crude and the diction was unrefined, they were preserved exactly according to the original text.

Those who hear this sutra and, with joy, faith, and delight, single-mindedly revere it, receive and uphold it, recite and chant it, proclaim and extol the names of all Buddhas and manifest the merits of the Tathāgatas, and widely propagate it, shall attain the stage of non-retrogression and swiftly accomplish the unsurpassed, true, and correct path; no number of heavenly Māras shall be able to destroy their resolve for the unsurpassed path.
In whatever place they are born, they shall adorn and purify Buddha-fields and always encounter the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
They will be upright and exquisite, with radiant and lustrous countenances, and will always be able to comprehend immeasurable wisdom.
Attaining unimpeded eloquence, he shall constantly expound the Great Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, becoming the foremost leader among the great assemblies.
When he later attains Buddhahood,
his buddha-field will be pure.
Among all Buddha-lands,
it shall be the most honored and foremost.

I vow that immeasurable sentient beings throughout the ten directions will universally recite and uphold it, so that they may understand the Tathāgata’s unimpeded wisdom and its towering merits, and likewise become like these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
The Sutra of Praising the Merits of All Buddhas, Scroll II.
